scenario: The Horni Polna Regional Hospital is preparing a CZK 180 million reconstruction of its internal medicine pavilion. In Starting up a project, the project manager submitted the project brief and proposed that the Project Board authorise the entire project on that basis straight away, with a single delivery stage covering the construction design, the construction, the fit-out and the move. She considers a separate initiation stage unnecessary, because a detailed technical design already exists from an earlier study.
question: Was it appropriate to propose omitting the initiation stage, and why?
options: No, because Manage by stages requires at least two management stages, the first of which is always the initiation stage.
Yes, because for projects with a completed study the Starting up a project process can be regarded as the project's initiation stage.
No, because PRINCE2 always requires at least three stages: initiation, delivery and a separate closing stage.
Yes, because tailoring allows the Manage by stages principle to be omitted for projects with a completed technical design.
explanation: The Manage by stages principle requires at least two management stages: the initiation stage and at least one delivery stage. Initiation is meant to create firm foundations (the PID, the full business case, the project plan) before the Project Board releases large resources; an existing study can shorten it but not replace it. Starting up a project is not a stage but a pre-project activity, and principles cannot be omitted through tailoring – only the way they are applied is adapted.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

scenario: The Horni Polna hospital is reconstructing its internal medicine pavilion. The technical phases are: design documentation (4 months), tendering for a contractor (3 months), construction (12 months) and fit-out with the move (2 months). By signing the contract with the contractor, the hospital will commit to expenditure of over CZK 150 million. In Initiating a project, the project manager is proposing how to divide the rest of the project into management stages.
question: Which division into management stages is most appropriate according to PRINCE2?
options: Place a stage boundary before the signing of the contract with the contractor, so that the Project Board re-verifies the justification before the big commitment.
Create stages of equal three-month length, because stage boundaries in PRINCE2 are a time-driven control and should come at regular intervals.
Make the management stages coincide exactly with the four technical phases, because management and technical stages in PRINCE2 must always coincide.
Keep a single delivery stage after initiation, because each additional stage boundary merely increases the Project Board's administrative burden.
explanation: Stage boundaries should lie at points where the Project Board needs to decide on the next commitment – typically before the signing of a large contract; the number and length of stages derive from risk, complexity, the planning horizon and key decisions. The end of a stage is an event-driven control, not a time-driven one (highlight reports, for example, are time-driven). Management stages may coincide with technical phases, but need not.

scenario: Moravske Strojirny a.s. is developing an ESG reporting tool that is to enable the company to meet in good time the statutory obligation to publish a verified ESG report for 2027. During the second delivery stage, a change in legislation was approved under which the obligation for companies of this size is postponed by two years; the main benefit stated in the business case – meeting the obligation without penalties – is thereby significantly weakened. The cost and time of the stage are, however, within tolerance. The project manager concluded that he does not have to report the change to anyone and continues according to the stage plan.
question: Was the project manager's decision appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the change threatens the justification of the project; the PM should therefore capture it as an issue, assess the impact on the business case and escalate it.
Yes, because as long as the stage is within cost and time tolerance, the PM decides alone and the Project Board learns of the legislative change only from the end stage report.
No, because in such a situation the PM should immediately stop the project himself and start the Closing a project process as a premature closure.
Yes, because the ongoing justification of the project is assessed by the business layer only at the benefits review, which takes place after the project ends.
explanation: The Ensure continued business justification principle applies throughout the project: when the assumptions behind the benefits change, the impact must be assessed and the Project Board decides whether the project continues, is changed or ends. A change in legislation is an issue of the event external to the project type; the PM captures it, assesses the impact on the business case and escalates it, even though cost and time are within tolerance. A premature closure is decided by the Project Board, not the PM.

scenario: The town of Valdov is starting a Citizen Portal project, which is to enable people to submit applications for parking permits and pay local fees online. Before assembling the project brief, the project manager Martin Horak asked the project office for the lessons reports from the previous electronic records management project, which had great difficulties with integrations. He also met the project manager of a similar portal in another town and recorded the recommendations he received in the lessons log.
question: Was the project manager's conduct appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because under Learn from experience, lessons from earlier projects and from other organisations are sought already at the start, not only at the end.
Yes, because in PRINCE2 lessons are collected exclusively at the start and at the closure of the project, when the lessons report is produced from the lessons log.
No, because lessons from other organisations' projects are not relevant to this project and are not recorded in the project's lessons log.
No, because the search for lessons begins only in Initiating a project, when the registers and logs that together form the project log are set up.
explanation: Learn from experience applies at the start, during and at the end of the project; in Starting up a project the Assess previous lessons activity serves this purpose. Lessons can be drawn from one's own projects as well as from other organisations, and they are recorded in the lessons log so that they can be acted on. The claim that lessons are collected only at the start and at the end is wrong – they are sought and applied continuously.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

scenario: Horal Sport a.s. is migrating its e-shop to a new cloud platform. In the second delivery stage, the head of the data team (a Team manager) discovered that the migration of product data repeatedly fails on the same character-encoding problem, and she found a procedure for preventing the error. The next two batches of the migration are scheduled in upcoming work packages. The Team manager noted that she will mention the experience only at the final lessons meeting when the project is closed.
question: Which course of action is most appropriate according to PRINCE2?
options: Pass the lesson immediately to the project manager so that he records it in the lessons log and applies it in the next work packages.
Leave the lesson until the end of the project, because during delivery Learn from experience applies only in the end stage reports.
Immediately produce a lessons report and send it to the business layer, because every lesson is assessed by the organisation's management.
Keep the lesson within the team, because it concerns technical work and the lessons log is intended only for lessons from project management.
explanation: Learn from experience applies throughout the project, and everyone, not just the project manager, should seek and share lessons. The lesson is recorded in the lessons log and used immediately in the next work packages so that the error is not repeated; waiting until the project is closed means losing its value. A lessons report for the business layer is produced at the end of the project (or stage), not for each individual lesson.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

scenario: In the reconstruction of the internal medicine pavilion at the Horni Polna hospital, the project has an established Project Board and approved role descriptions for all roles, including the Team manager, who is the site manager of the external contractor. The construction takes place alongside operating wards. Ward nurses repeatedly complain that they learn about noisy work and water and electricity shutdowns only when they begin. The site manager claims he has no obligation to deal with hospital staff, because it is not in his role description.
question: Which step by the project manager best applies the Define roles, responsibilities and relationships principle?
options: Agree with the site manager and the head nurse on contact persons and coordination meetings, because the principle also includes building relationships.
Propose placing the site manager on the Project Board as an additional Senior supplier, so that he has the authority to deal with hospital staff.
Leave everything unchanged, because the principle is satisfied by every role having an approved role description and being listed in the team structure.
Ask the business layer to amend the contract with the contractor, because relationships with external suppliers in the project are governed only by the commercial contract.
explanation: In PRINCE2 7, the Define roles, responsibilities and relationships principle includes, besides roles and responsibilities, building relationships between the people in the project and with stakeholders, both internal and external. Approved role descriptions alone are not enough when collaboration between construction and operations does not work. Placing the site manager on the Project Board would mix the delivery level with the directing level and would not solve the communication problem.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

scenario: In the Citizen Portal project of the town of Valdov, the Project Board approved the stage plan of the second stage with a cost tolerance of ±10% and a time tolerance of ±2 weeks. The Executive, the town clerk, nevertheless requires the project manager to submit every purchase over CZK 20,000 to her for approval. Together with the Senior user, she also attends the weekly meetings of the supplier's development team, where they assign tasks to the developers directly.
question: Is this way of managing by the Project Board appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the Project Board manages by exception: within the stage tolerance it leaves day-to-day management to the PM and decides when a breach of it is threatened.
Yes, because the Executive is responsible for the business case and must therefore personally approve every project expenditure as part of managing the stage.
Yes, because Manage by exception allows the Project Board to determine which individual expenditures and tasks it will approve itself and which it will not.
No, because the cost tolerance is set by the business layer, and the Project Board therefore must not interfere in any way with the drawing of the project budget during the stage.
explanation: Manage by exception means that each level delegates authority to the level below through tolerances: the Project Board sets the stage tolerances, the PM manages day-to-day work within them and escalates when he forecasts a breach. The Executive is responsible for the business case, but that does not mean approving individual purchases or assigning tasks to developers – that would bypass both the PM and the Team manager. The project tolerance is set by the business layer, but the stage tolerance is set precisely by the Project Board.

image.alt: A chain of the business layer, the Project Board, the Project manager and the Team manager: tolerances are set from the top down and exceptions are escalated from the bottom up.

scenario: Horal Sport a.s. is migrating its e-shop to a new platform. The implementation partner submitted the plan for the second stage as a list of activities (analysis, programming, testing, meetings) with person-day counts. The Senior user, the e-commerce director, objected at a Project Board meeting that from the plan he cannot tell what exactly will be finished at the end of the stage and against what he will be able to accept it.
question: Which step by the project manager best applies the Focus on products principle?
options: Have the stage's products described in product descriptions with quality specifications and derive the plan from them, because planning starts with products.
Supplement the plan with a detailed Gantt chart of all activities, because a precise schedule of activities clearly and completely defines the scope of the stage.
Require the reporting of hours worked in the checkpoint reports, against which the progress of the stage will be measured against the plan.
Ask the Senior user to approve the list of activities, because he is responsible for accepting the products and his agreement will confirm the stage plan.
explanation: Focus on products means defining products (what is to be delivered and what characteristics it should have) before planning activities; product descriptions with quality specifications then guide planning, quality control and acceptance. A detailed Gantt chart merely schedules the activities more precisely but does not say what the result will be and against what it will be accepted. Progress is judged by completed and approved products, not by hours consumed.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

scenario: The town of Valdov is carrying out a small internal project: moving meeting-room bookings to a new intranet module (budget CZK 400,000, a team of four, three months). The project manager proposed that the PID be kept as a page on the intranet wiki, that highlight reports take the form of short weekly emails and that checkpoints take place verbally at the Monday meeting. These adaptations are described in the PID, which the Project Board approved; the stages and tolerances are retained.
question: Is this adaptation of the method appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because the form and formality of products can be adapted, provided their purpose is preserved and all the principles continue to apply.
Yes, because in small projects management products and the related practices can be omitted, and neither a PID nor regular reporting is necessary.
No, because management products must always have the form and content given by the templates in Appendix A, so that the project can later be audited.
No, because checkpoint reports must always be in writing, otherwise they cannot be submitted to the Project Board for assessment and approval.
explanation: Tailoring adapts practices, processes, products and their formality to the size and complexity of the project – a PID as a wiki, brief emailed highlight reports or verbal checkpoints are typical examples. The condition is that the purpose of the products remains fulfilled (the Project Board has enough information to manage by exception) and that all seven principles continue to apply. Practices are not omitted, only reasonably simplified; moreover, checkpoint reports belong to the project manager, not the Project Board.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

scenario: Horal Sport a.s. is migrating its e-shop to a new platform. The implementation partner's development teams work in two-week sprints and each sprint ends with a demonstration of the finished features to users. The backlog changes continually after the demonstrations, so the team can plan reliably only about three months ahead, and in the middle of the project a decision is due on moving customers to the new platform. The project manager nevertheless proposed that the whole remainder of the project after the initiation stage consist of a single ten-month stage: the sprint reviews, he says, fully replace the stage boundaries and the Project Board would meet again only when the project is closed.
question: Is this proposal in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: No, because a sprint review is not a substitute for stage boundaries; sprints run inside stages, whose length is determined by the planning horizon and key decisions.
Yes, because with iterative-incremental delivery, tailoring can omit the principles that do not suit this delivery method.
Yes, because the sprint review provides ongoing control by the Senior user and the Project Board is needed only for the closure decision.
No, because PRINCE2 does not support iterative-incremental delivery and the implementation partner must switch to linear-sequential delivery for the whole project.
explanation: Manage by stages applies also with iterative-incremental delivery: timeboxes (sprints) are planned inside management stages, whose number and length derive from the planning horizon, risks and points where the Project Board needs to decide – here from the roughly three-month horizon and the decision on moving customers. A sprint review is a useful control at the delivery level, but it does not replace the stage boundary at which the Project Board assesses results, the business case and the next plan. Principles cannot be omitted through tailoring, and PRINCE2 7 explicitly supports linear, iterative and hybrid delivery.

scenario: The town of Valdov is developing the Citizen Portal for online applications and fee payments with the external company SoftCity. In Initiating a project, the project manager agreed with the project management team on adaptations to the method: highlight reports will take the form of an online dashboard, the issue register and the risk register will be kept in a single tool, and stage boundaries will be aligned with the town's budget year. The Senior supplier asks where these decisions will be recorded and who will confirm them.
question: How should the tailoring decisions be handled according to PRINCE2?
options: Describe them in the PID as the result of the Agree tailoring requirements activity, because the PID is approved by the Project Board when authorising the project.
Enter them in the project brief, which is maintained throughout the project and serves as the basic agreement on how the project is managed.
Record them only in the project manager's daily log, because they are informal working arrangements that do not require the Project Board's consent.
State them in the lessons log, because tailoring is above all a lesson for future projects, which the business layer will assess at the end.
explanation: Tailoring requirements are agreed in Initiating a project (the Agree tailoring requirements activity) and documented in the PID, which the Project Board approves when authorising the project – that is how the adaptations of the method are formally confirmed. The project brief is created in Starting up a project and is replaced by the PID after initiation, so it is no longer maintained. The daily log serves the PM for informal records, not for agreements on how the project is managed.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records, from the daily log to the product register.

scenario: The migration of Horal Sport a.s.'s e-shop is one of the projects of the Digital Horal programme. The programme has its own approach to risk management, including uniform probability and impact scales, and monthly reporting to the programme office in a uniform format. While preparing the PID, the project manager proposes introducing his own, more detailed risk scales and his own report format, because the programme scales seem too coarse to him.
question: Which course of action is most appropriate for this project?
options: Build on the programme's standards and describe in the PID how the project adopts or supplements them, so that the risks and reports can be consolidated in the programme.
Prepare an entirely separate risk management approach, because every PRINCE2 project must have its own scales independent of its surroundings.
Omit risk management in the project, because the programme manages the project's risks on its behalf, and the Risk practice therefore need not be applied in the project.
Adopt the programme's risk scales but keep its own report format, because the project's reporting to the programme is not subject to tailoring.
explanation: Tailor to suit the project includes adapting to the project's environment – if the project is part of a programme, it should adopt the programme's standards and describe in the PID how it applies or supplements them. Different scales and formats would make it impossible to consolidate risks and reports at programme level. Practices are not omitted through tailoring, only adapted; even within a programme, the project must identify and manage its own risks.

scenario: The Horni Polna hospital manages all investments according to an internal directive that uses its own terms: instead of business case, "investment intent"; instead of Project Board, "investment committee"; and instead of stage, "investment phase". The project manager of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction proposed keeping these terms in the project and added a conversion table to PRINCE2 terms to the PID. The Senior supplier from the construction company objects that without the original terminology it is not a PRINCE2 project.
question: Is the project manager's approach appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because tailoring allows the organisation's terminology to be adopted, provided the roles and products fulfil their purpose and the link to PRINCE2 is clear.
Yes, because terminology in PRINCE2 does not matter, and the investment committee therefore need not fulfil all the responsibilities of the Project Board.
No, because applying PRINCE2 requires using exclusively the method's official English names of roles, management products and processes.
No, because tailoring may rename management products but not roles, whose names are fixed in PRINCE2.
explanation: Adopting the organisation's terminology is a typical form of tailoring – what matters is that the renamed roles and products fulfil their purpose and it is clear what they correspond to in PRINCE2. A project is a PRINCE2 project because it applies all seven principles, not because it uses particular names. The "investment committee" must therefore fulfil all the responsibilities of the Project Board; it is merely named differently.

scenario: Moravske Strojirny a.s. is developing an ESG reporting tool. The project has a Project Board with an Executive, a Senior user and a Senior supplier and is divided into four stages, at the end of each of which the Project Board always assesses the updated business case. Tolerances are set for each stage and the project manager submits regular highlight reports. Lessons from the previous accounting consolidation project were reflected in the plans. The teams, however, receive only task lists: for no output is it described what characteristics it should have and against what it will be accepted, and users will see the results only at the end of the project.
question: Which PRINCE2 principle is NOT sufficiently applied in this project?
options: Focus on products
Manage by exception
Learn from experience
Ensure continued business justification
explanation: The scenario lacks a definition of products: outputs have no described characteristics (quality specifications) or method of acceptance, and the teams work from task lists. This contradicts the Focus on products principle, under which product descriptions guide planning, quality control and acceptance. Manage by exception is fulfilled by tolerances and reporting, Learn from experience by adopting lessons, and Ensure continued business justification by assessing the business case at the end of each stage.

image.alt: Overview of the seven PRINCE2 7 principles with their names and a short explanation.

scenario: In the ESG reporting project of Moravske Strojirny, the data integrations with 12 plants will be carried out by analysts from the plants who have not yet worked on any project. The project manager has therefore set weekly checkpoint reports for their work packages instead of the usual monthly ones, prepared more detailed work package descriptions and set a narrower time tolerance. For the experienced team of the external consultant he kept monthly checkpoints.
question: Is this adaptation appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because tailoring also takes into account the capabilities of the team, and a less experienced team may need more frequent control and more detailed work assignments.
No, because the frequency of checkpoint reports is fixed in PRINCE2 and must be the same for all work packages and teams within the project.
No, because tailoring may only reduce the formality of the method, and adding controls beyond normal practice is therefore not permissible.
Yes, because Manage by exception requires the project manager to approve every task of the members of inexperienced teams.
explanation: The Tailor to suit the project principle requires adapting the method to, among other things, the capabilities of the team – for an inexperienced team it is reasonable to choose more frequent checkpoints, more detailed work package descriptions and narrower tolerances. The frequency of checkpoint reports and the work package tolerance are set by the PM in the work package description for each package separately. Tailoring may reduce or increase formality; managing by exception does not mean, however, that the PM would approve individual tasks.

scenario: The town of Valdov is introducing the Citizen Portal for online applications for parking permits and fee payments; the counters at the office will remain unchanged. A rumour is spreading among seniors in one district of the town that the counters will be abolished, and the local committee has drawn up a petition. The project manager therefore included the seniors from this part of the town in the stakeholder map and planned an information meeting for them. A team member objects that the change will objectively not affect them and that they are therefore not stakeholders.
question: Was it appropriate to include the seniors among the stakeholders, and why?
options: Yes, because a stakeholder is also someone who merely believes they are affected by the project, and their concerns need to be addressed through communication.
Yes, because all the town's residents are stakeholders, and the project must therefore involve every group to the same extent.
No, because stakeholders are only those who can directly influence the project, and the seniors have no authority in the project.
No, because communication with the public is handled by the business layer and does not belong in the project's communication management approach.
explanation: A stakeholder is anyone who can affect or be affected by the project – including those who merely believe they are affected. A mistaken perception can provoke resistance that endangers acceptance of the results, so it is right to include the seniors among the stakeholders and to determine in the communication management approach how to communicate with them. This does not mean that every group of residents would have to be involved to the same extent – the degree of involvement is governed by their influence and by how much they are affected.

scenario: In the reconstruction of the internal medicine pavilion at the Horni Polna hospital, the project manager prepared a draft communication management approach. It contains a monthly email newsletter about the construction for all hospital employees, highlight reports for the Project Board and press releases for the public. The head nurse of the internal medicine ward points out that the nurses have nowhere to raise questions about planned shutdowns and patient relocations, so the project will not learn about their problems.
question: How should the project manager best amend the draft?
options: Add channels and dates for staff feedback, e.g. regular meetings with the construction team, because communication should be two-way.
Increase the newsletter frequency to weekly, because sending information more often will in itself ensure that staff are well informed.
Convert the nurses' questions into the issue management approach, because every question about the project is an issue decided by the change authority.
Leave the draft unchanged and leave staff questions to the Senior user, who will resolve them within his line outside the project.
explanation: The communication management approach determines the means and frequency of communication with the project ecosystem and also how feedback is obtained from it – it is a managed two-way flow of information. A one-way newsletter, even a more frequent one, will not allow the nurses to raise questions and the project will not learn of their concerns. Questions are not automatically issues; the issue management approach serves to manage issues and changes to the baseline, not communication with affected people.

scenario: Horal Sport a.s. is migrating its e-shop to a new platform. After go-live, warehouse staff will pick orders using new handheld terminals and according to amended procedures, and customer-line operators will work in a new system. The project manager wants to describe in the PID how these people will be prepared for the transition, how their readiness will be verified before go-live and how resistance to the change will be handled.
question: In which part of the PID does this description best belong?
options: In the change management approach, because it describes how the project will support the transition of people and the organisation from the current to the target state.
In the issue management approach, because all changes in the project, including changes to warehouse working procedures, are managed by its procedure.
In the quality management approach, because training warehouse staff is a quality method by which the fulfilment of the acceptance criteria is verified.
In the commercial management approach, because the terminals are supplied by an external supplier and preparing people to use them is part of the contract.
explanation: Change management in PRINCE2 7 means managing the transition of the organisation and people from the current to the target state; how the project will support this transition, including preparing people and dealing with their concerns, is described by the change management approach in the PID. The issue management approach concerns managing issues and changes to the baseline (change control), not organisational change. Confusing these two terms leads to the preparation of people for the transition not being planned at all.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records, from the daily log to the product register.

scenario: In the ESG reporting project at Moravske Strojirny, the team consists of analysts from various plants, controllers from head office and external consultants. None of them reports line-wise to the project manager, and they work on the project alongside their regular jobs. The PM sends out tasks by e-mail with deadlines, reports every missed deadline to the person's superior and does not allow any discussion of ways of working at meetings. Team engagement is dropping significantly and two analysts have asked to be released from the project.
question: Is the project manager's approach appropriate, and why?
options: No, because in a temporary team spanning the organisation the PM has weak formal authority and should lead through influence, collaboration and continuous feedback.
Yes, because the PM is responsible for the day-to-day management of the project, and assigning work according to agreed procedures is the core of the PM's role in the project.
Yes, because project team members are subordinate to the project manager for the duration of the project, so the PM can instruct them directly what work to do.
No, because the PM should not deal with team members directly but only through Team managers, who manage the individual work packages on the PM's behalf.
explanation: PRINCE2 7 distinguishes between management (managing the delivery of tasks according to agreed procedures) and leadership (motivating and influencing people towards goals). In a temporary team spanning departments and organisations the PM's formal authority is weak, and a "command and control" style therefore leads to a loss of engagement; it is more appropriate to lead through influence, collaboration, involving the team in planning and frequent feedback. The PM does manage the day-to-day work, but needs leadership for this as well, not just orders; moreover, the Team manager role is optional.

scenario: The town of Valdov is developing a Citizen Portal with an external company, SoftCity. The project manager has organised a series of workshops in which officials from the transport department and a group of citizens, including seniors and business owners, design the forms and the application process together with the developers. The SoftCity development team leader objects that the workshops slow down development and that the developers could design the forms faster on their own based on the specification.
question: Is involving officials and citizens in the design appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because co-creation with users and key influencers improves the design of products and increases their acceptance.
Yes, because the involved citizens thereby take over responsibility for accepting the portal, which the Senior user would otherwise have to bear for the whole project.
No, because user requirements are specified exclusively by the Senior user and other users should not be involved in designing the project's products.
No, because in PRINCE2 co-creation is intended only for designing the team's ways of working, not for designing the project's products themselves.
explanation: Co-creation means that users and key influencers help design both products and ways of working; the result is a better design and greater willingness to accept the change. The Senior user is responsible for how user requirements are captured, which does not rule out involving other users but actually supports it. Involving citizens does not shift responsibility for acceptance – the acceptance of the project product is led by the Senior user.

scenario: In the ESG reporting project at Moravske Strojirny, the Senior supplier is the IT director, who provides the internal developers. During planning of the second stage it turned out that nobody in the team has experience connecting the plants' production systems to the data warehouse. Without this competence the key product of the stage – automatic collection of energy consumption data – cannot be delivered. The project manager is considering how to handle the situation.
question: Which course of action is the most appropriate according to PRINCE2?
options: Assess the gap in the team's capabilities and agree with the Senior supplier on closing it through training or by adding people, because the Senior supplier provides the resources.
Accept the gap, record it in the lessons log as a lesson for building the team of the next project and continue according to plan.
Lower the quality specification of the automatic data collection so that the current team can cope with it, and record the adjustment in the PM's daily log.
Transfer the provision of competences to the Senior user, because the Senior user is responsible for the capabilities needed to create the products that users will use.
explanation: An effective team needs adequate team capability as well as individual competences, and identified gaps should be actively addressed – through training, recruitment or by adding people. The Senior supplier provides the supplier-side resources, so it is right to agree with them on closing the gap. Lowering the quality specification without proper change control would bypass issue management and jeopardise the purpose of the product.

scenario: The reconstruction of the internal medicine pavilion at Horni Polna Hospital is carried out by a construction company used to quick verbal agreements directly on site. The hospital, by contrast, has a very formal culture built on patient safety, hygiene regulations and written approval of interventions in operations. The project manager therefore proposed that interventions in the ward's operations be approved according to the hospital's rules, and agreed an accelerated procedure with the site manager: the request is submitted electronically and the ward nurse confirms it within 24 hours. The construction company's director (Senior supplier) objects that the project is a temporary organisation and should therefore set up its own, faster way of working.
question: Is the project manager's approach appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because the project culture should be aligned with the hospital's organisational ecosystem and differences between cultures must be bridged.
No, because the project is a temporary organisation and can therefore set its own culture independently of the hospital's customs and rules.
Yes, because the project culture is determined by the chosen delivery approach, and in this case that is governed by the hospital's operating rules.
No, because the project culture is set by the business layer in the project mandate and the project manager must not adapt it in any way.
explanation: Culture is shared values, attitudes and working habits; different organisations involved in a project may have different cultures. PRINCE2 7 stresses that the project culture should be aligned with the organisational ecosystem – here with the hospital's safety culture – and that differences between the cultures of the hospital and the supplier need to be actively bridged, which the agreed accelerated procedure also serves. The temporary nature of the project does not entitle it to ignore the customs of the environment into which the project delivers change, and the project culture is determined neither by the delivery approach nor by the project mandate.

scenario: The Horal Sport a.s. e-shop migration involves a product team at the Prague head office, developers of an implementation partner from Brno working mostly remotely, and testers of a subcontractor from Vietnam. During the first delivery stage misunderstandings multiply, the teams blame each other for mistakes and communicate with each other only through tickets. The project manager is looking for an appropriate step.
question: Which step best matches the PRINCE2 recommendation for leading teams?
options: Strengthen trust and cohesion between the locations, e.g. through joint online meetings, agreed rules of collaboration and occasional face-to-face meetings.
Require all teams to work at the Prague head office, because PRINCE2 considers a shared workplace a condition of an effective team.
Limit communication between teams to formal checkpoint reports, to eliminate the misunderstandings that arise in informal communication channels.
Divide the work so that the locations do not depend on each other at all, because then there is no need to address collaboration or communication between teams.
explanation: PRINCE2 7 stresses that effective teams need trust and social cohesion regardless of whether they work together in one place, virtually or in a hybrid manner; communication needs to be adapted to the hybrid arrangement and cultural differences should also be taken into account. A shared workplace is not a condition. Limiting communication to formal reports would deepen the mistrust – informal communication is just as important for collaboration.

scenario: Because of the reconstruction of the internal medicine pavilion at Horni Polna Hospital, the ward is to move to temporary premises in another building for 14 months. The nurses are worried about longer patient transfers and worse working conditions, and several of them are considering leaving. The Executive proposes that the hospital director simply order the move, because it is an operational matter outside the project.
question: Which course of action is the most appropriate according to PRINCE2?
options: Involve the nurses early in planning the move, explain the reasons for and impacts of the change, and address their concerns within the change management approach.
Order the move as the Executive proposes, because the impacts on employees are a matter of the hospital's regular operations, not of the project.
Record the nurses' concerns in the risk register as a threat with the response accept and not actively deal with them further until the risk actually materialises.
Postpone dealing with the concerns until project closure, when the users' acceptance of the change and their training are addressed during the handover of products into operation.
explanation: In PRINCE2 7 a project delivers change that affects people in regular operations; the affected people therefore need to be involved, the reasons for and impacts of the change explained to them and their concerns actively addressed – the approach is described in the change management approach. An order issued without involvement can lead to resistance and departures that endanger both operations and the project's benefits. Postponing work with people until closure is too late: the transition must be prepared continuously.

scenario: The town of Valdov is preparing to launch the Citizen Portal. The project manager is drawing up the communication management approach and preparing an entry for the officials of the transport department who will process applications from the portal. The officials are anxious about the new system and have so far learned about the project only from unofficial reports.
question: Which entry is the most appropriate for the communication management approach?
options: Transport department officials: monthly meeting with a portal demonstration and a project page on the intranet; questions via a designated contact person; PM responsible.
Transport department officials: there is a threat that they will reject the new system and keep processing applications the old way; risk owner Senior user, response reduce.
Transport department officials: before launch they complete eight hours of training and their readiness for the new way of working is verified; Senior user responsible.
Transport department officials: a request to modify a form is assessed by the change authority within five working days and the decision is recorded in the issue register.
explanation: The communication management approach describes with whom, by what means and how often the project communicates and how it obtains feedback from these people; the correct entry therefore states the target audience, channels, frequency, route for questions and responsibility. An entry about the threat of rejection belongs in the risk register, and training with readiness verification belongs rather in the change management approach. The time limit for assessing requests for change is part of the issue management approach.

scenario: The town of Valdov's Citizen Portal has been tested and is ready for handover into operation. The Senior user, the head of the transport department, declared that the project's task is to deliver working software; whether the officials actually start using the portal and whether application processing time shortens is, in his view, a matter for regular operations after the project ends. He therefore refused to release the officials for training and a pilot run before launch.
question: Is the Senior user's attitude in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: No, because the Senior user is responsible for the handover and adoption of products on the users' side, on which the achievement of outcomes and benefits depends.
Yes, because the project is responsible only for outputs, and the organisation's business layer is solely responsible for changes in user behaviour after handover.
No, because the Senior supplier is responsible for training and the pilot run and must prepare the users to take over the products on their own and at their own expense.
Yes, because in PRINCE2 benefits are measured only after the project ends, and preparing users therefore does not belong in the project's scope.
explanation: Project outputs deliver outcomes and benefits only if users accept them and start using them; PRINCE2 7 therefore emphasises the transition of people to the new state, and the Senior user is responsible for the handover and adoption of products on the users' side. Releasing the officials for training and a pilot run is therefore within the Senior user's responsibility. Benefits are indeed often measured only after the project, but the conditions for achieving them must be created by the project.

scenario: The ESG reporting tool of Moravske Strojirny needs monthly data on energy consumption and waste from all 12 plants. The directors of three plants, who are not members of the project management team, refuse to supply the data because, in their view, it takes their people away from production. The project manager repeatedly tried to persuade them, without success. He therefore asked the Executive, the company's finance director, to deal with the situation at his level.
question: Was it appropriate to turn to the Executive, and why?
options: Yes, because the Project Board manages relationships at the interface between the project and organisational ecosystems and the Executive has the authority to deal with plant management.
Yes, because collecting data from the plants is the Executive's personal responsibility as owner of the business case and the project manager should not deal with it.
No, because the Project Board comments on the project only at stage boundaries and between them the project manager must resolve all difficulties alone.
No, because plant directors do not belong to the project management team and are therefore not stakeholders that the project would have to deal with.
explanation: Among other things, the Project Board in PRINCE2 7 manages relationships at the interface between the project and organisational ecosystems; unlike the PM, the Executive has the authority to deal with plant management. Moreover, the Board is not limited to stage boundaries – within Give ongoing direction it responds to the PM's requests for advice between them as well. Plant directors significantly influence the project and are therefore key stakeholders even though they have no formal role.

scenario: The project manager of the Moravske Strojirny ESG reporting project is mapping the project ecosystem. They are considering the finance department, controlling, 12 plants, the data platform supplier, an external auditor who will verify the ESG report, and trade unions concerned about monitoring employee performance. The Senior user proposes limiting the map to members of the project management team to keep it clear.
question: Which approach to defining the project ecosystem is the most appropriate according to PRINCE2?
options: Include the involved or affected parts of the business, users and suppliers, because even the auditor and the trade unions can significantly influence the project.
Limit the map to the project management team, because the project ecosystem consists only of people who have a formal role in the project structure.
Include the whole organisational ecosystem including competitors and regulators, which is identical to the project ecosystem in PRINCE2.
Include only the users' departments, because the supplier and the auditor are outside the company and the trade unions have no formal role in the project.
explanation: The project ecosystem consists of the parts of the business, users and suppliers that are involved in the project or affected by it; it lies within organisational ecosystems, and key stakeholders are often found right at its boundary. Limiting the map to the project management team would leave out people who can significantly influence the project, e.g. the trade unions or the auditor. The organisational ecosystem is a broader concept – it includes the whole organisation and its external relationships.

scenario: In the Horal Sport a.s. e-shop migration project, the Project Board receives a highlight report every two weeks. The head of the customer service line, who is not a member of the Project Board, needs to know in good time about the testing and launch dates so that she can plan operators' shifts. She therefore asked the project manager to send her the highlight reports as well.
question: How should the project manager proceed according to PRINCE2?
options: Check whether the communication management approach allows it and, where appropriate, add her there as a recipient of highlight reports.
Refuse, because the highlight report is intended exclusively for the Project Board and under no circumstances is it provided to other persons in PRINCE2.
Send her the Team managers' checkpoint reports instead of highlight reports, because they contain more detailed information about the progress of testing.
Recommend that she become a member of the Project Board as an additional Senior user, because only board members can receive highlight reports.
explanation: The highlight report is primarily intended for the Project Board, but the communication management approach may stipulate that other stakeholders receive it as well. The head of the customer service line is a key stakeholder for preparing the launch, so it is appropriate to include her among the recipients in line with this approach. Checkpoint reports are reports from Team managers to the project manager and do not serve to inform other parties.

scenario: Moravske Strojirny a.s. is preparing the business case for the ESG reporting tool. The Executive, the finance director, wants the business case to show clearly the chain from project outputs through capabilities and outcomes to benefits. The project manager therefore goes through the items proposed by the team and sorts them.
question: Which of the proposed items is an outcome in the PRINCE2 sense?
options: Controllers compile the quarterly ESG overview from a single data source without manually merging spreadsheets.
A data connector that links the production systems of all 12 plants to the central ESG data repository.
A reduction in the cost of external consultants in preparing the ESG report by CZK 1.2 million per year compared with today.
A complete tool with connectors, a calculation methodology and trained users, ready for deployment.
explanation: An outcome is a change in real behaviour or circumstances that occurs when new capabilities start to be used – here controllers work differently than before. The connector is an output, a complete tool ready for deployment is a capability made up of outputs, and the cost reduction is a measurable benefit that results from the outcome. The chain in PRINCE2 7 leads from outputs through capabilities and outcomes to benefits and business objectives.

image.alt: A chain of outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits and business objectives, with a definition and an example for each link.

scenario: The business case of the ESG reporting tool of Moravske Strojirny counts on savings on external consultants. However, after the tool is introduced, foremen in all 12 plants will have to enter waste data manually every month, which according to measurements in the pilot plant takes them approximately two extra hours per month. The project manager stated this fact in the business case as a dis-benefit. The Senior supplier objects that negative impacts belong in the risk register.
question: Was it appropriate to state this fact in the business case, and why?
options: Yes, because it is an expected measurable deterioration resulting from a project outcome, i.e. a dis-benefit, which is always assessed together with the benefits.
Yes, because every negative impact of the project on employees is reported in the business case as part of the cost of delivering the project.
No, because every negative impact of the project is a threat and is therefore recorded and managed in the risk register with an assigned risk owner.
No, because it is a problem that has already manifested in the pilot plant and therefore belongs in the issue register as an issue that needs to be resolved.
explanation: A dis-benefit is a measurable deterioration that results from a project outcome and is perceived negatively by some stakeholder; unlike a risk it is not uncertain but expected. It therefore belongs in the business case alongside the benefits, so that the Project Board assesses a balanced picture. The risk register serves for uncertain events, and the pilot measurement does not mean an issue to be resolved – it is a known consequence of the new way of working.

image.alt: A chain of outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits and business objectives, with a definition and an example for each link.

scenario: Horal Sport a.s. is migrating its e-shop to a cloud platform. In the third stage the platform provider announced a 30% increase in licence prices from next year, which will significantly extend the payback period of the investment. The project manager assessed the impact, informed the Project Board and updated the business case in Managing a stage boundary. The Senior user objects that the business case was approved as a baseline and should no longer be changed until the end of the project.
question: Was the project manager's approach in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: Yes, because the business case must be maintained throughout the project: the impact of changes is assessed continuously and the document is updated at stage boundaries.
Yes, because the business case is the project manager's working document, which the PM can modify at any time without the Project Board's knowledge.
No, because an approved business case is a baseline, and updating it would require new authorization of the entire project by the Project Board.
No, because the impact of licence prices on the payback will be assessed by the business layer only as part of a benefits review held after the project ends.
explanation: The business case management technique includes the steps develop, check, maintain and confirm benefits; maintaining means continuously assessing the impact of issues, risks and changes on the project's justification and updating the business case at the stage boundary (Update the business case in Managing a stage boundary). A baseline does not mean that the document must not be changed, but that it is changed in a controlled way – the updated business case is assessed by the Project Board when authorising the next stage. If the impact of the price increase exceeded tolerances, the PM would escalate the matter immediately.

scenario: Horni Polna Hospital is reconstructing the internal medicine pavilion. The business case lists these benefits: a reduction in the average length of hospital stay by 0.5 days and a 20% reduction in hospital-acquired infections, which will show up only a year after the pavilion opens. The Executive proposed that the head physician of internal medicine, who is the Senior user on the Project Board, be responsible for achieving these benefits. The project manager objects that the Executive, as owner of the business case, must be responsible for the benefits.
question: Is the Executive's proposal in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: Yes, because the Senior user specifies the benefits and is responsible for demonstrating that the anticipated benefits are actually achieved.
Yes, because the head physician will verify the achievement of benefits as part of project assurance, which the project manager performs on behalf of the Senior user.
No, because the Executive, as owner of the business case, is personally responsible for achieving the benefits, and this responsibility therefore cannot be transferred.
No, because the project manager, who prepared the benefits management approach, is responsible for measuring and achieving the benefits.
explanation: The Senior user specifies the benefits on which the business case rests and is responsible for demonstrating that the anticipated benefits are actually achieved – they represent those who will use the project's results. The Executive owns the business case and is responsible for the ongoing justification of the project, but this does not remove the Senior user's responsibility for achieving the benefits. Benefits reviews after the project ends are planned in the benefits management approach and carried out by the business layer; moreover, the PM must not perform project assurance.

scenario: The project manager of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction at Horni Polna Hospital is comparing two heating options. The gas boiler is CZK 6 million cheaper. The heat pump is more expensive but still within the project's cost tolerance and is the only one that meets the emissions reduction objective, which is listed in the business case as a sustainability objective with a tolerance. The manager recommended the gas boiler to the Project Board because it is the cheapest.
question: Was the project manager's recommendation appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the preferred option should keep all seven performance targets within tolerance, including sustainability, not just cost.
Yes, because the business case compares only costs and benefits and sustainability is addressed separately in the quality management approach.
Yes, because the choice of option is decided primarily by the cost tolerance that the business layer set for the Project Board for the whole project.
No, because the option with the best sustainability impact must always be chosen, regardless of its costs, benefits and other targets.
explanation: In PRINCE2 7, sustainability objectives and their tolerances are taken into account in the business case; the preferred option is the one that keeps all seven performance targets (benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk) within tolerance, not necessarily the cheapest. The gas boiler would breach the emissions reduction objective, whereas the heat pump is still within the cost tolerance. Sustainability also does not mean a choice "at any cost" – it is balanced against the other targets.

image.alt: Two columns: the seven PRINCE2 7 practices and the seven performance targets, including sustainability.

scenario: The Horal Sport a.s. e-shop migration is part of the Digital Horal programme, whose business case counts on a 25% growth in online revenue. During initiation the project manager proposed that the project would have no justification of its own and that the Project Board would not deal with it at stage boundaries, because the justification is provided by the programme.
question: Which statement about the justification of this project is in line with PRINCE2?
options: The justification may be based on the programme's business case, but it must hold throughout the project and the Project Board verifies it at each authorization.
Because the programme provides the justification, the Ensure continued business justification principle does not apply to projects within a programme.
The project should have a completely separate business case with its own investment appraisal, regardless of what the programme's business case contains.
The project's business case is owned by the programme manager, who must therefore always hold the Executive role on this project's Project Board.
explanation: The Ensure continued business justification principle applies to projects within a programme as well: the justification may rely on the programme's business case, but it must exist throughout the project and the Project Board verifies it at each authorization. A completely separate business case independent of the programme is not necessary, because it would duplicate the programme's justification. Who holds the Executive role is determined by the business layer – the programme manager may be that person, but need not be.

scenario: The town of Valdov's Citizen Portal is completed, tested and the transport department has taken it into use. The main benefit – shortening the processing time of a parking permit application from 15 to 3 days – can, according to the benefits management approach, be reliably measured only after a year of operation. The Executive proposes keeping the project open until all benefits have been demonstrated, to make sure they are actually achieved.
question: Is the Executive's proposal in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: No, because the project ends with the handover of accepted products and later benefits are verified through reviews according to the benefits management approach.
Yes, because the Ensure continued business justification principle requires the project to last until all benefits from the business case are confirmed.
No, because after the project ends benefits are no longer measured and their realisation is assessed in the end project report at closure.
Yes, because the Senior user cannot take over the project product before all benefits listed in the business case have been demonstrated.
explanation: Many benefits show up only after the project is closed; in Closing a project the benefits achieved so far are assessed and the benefits management approach is updated with post-project benefits reviews, which are carried out by the business layer. Keeping the project open would needlessly tie up the project team and costs, even though the products have already been handed over and accepted. The Ensure continued business justification principle concerns the duration of the project, not the period after it ends.

scenario: The project manager of the town of Valdov's Citizen Portal is preparing the project benefits management approach in Initiating a project. The main expected benefit is shortening the processing time of parking permit applications. The Senior user, the head of the transport department, points out that nobody currently knows exactly how long processing takes.
question: Which entry is the most appropriate for the benefits management approach?
options: Application processing time: baseline value measured before launch, target 3 days, measured by the transport department quarterly, Senior user responsible, reviews also after the project.
Parking permit application form: data validation, electronic signature and card payment; reviewed by a transport department clerk, approved by the Senior user.
There is a threat that citizens will use the portal less than the business case assumes and processing time will not shorten; risk owner Senior user, response reduce.
Transport department officials will be informed about the progress of the project once a month at the department meeting and on the project's intranet page.
explanation: The benefits management approach describes how and when benefits are measured, who is responsible for them, what baseline value they start from and when benefits reviews take place, including reviews after the project ends. Without measuring the starting state before launch it will not be possible to demonstrate the shortening of processing time. The other entries belong elsewhere: the description of the form in a product description, the threat in the risk register and informing the officials in the communication management approach.

scenario: From 2027 Moravske Strojirny a.s. is required by law to issue a verified ESG report. The finance director, appointed by the Executive of the ESG reporting project, declared that a business case is not needed because the project is mandatory and its implementation is not open to discussion. Three options are being considered: extending the existing ERP, a specialised cloud tool, or outsourcing the preparation of the report to a consultant.
question: Is the Executive's attitude in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: No, because even a mandatory project must have a business case, which justifies the choice of option and makes it possible to verify that the project remains justified.
Yes, because a legal obligation is in itself a sufficient justification, and the Ensure continued business justification principle therefore does not apply.
Yes, because for mandatory projects a decision of the business layer, recorded with its rationale in the project mandate, is sufficient instead of a business case.
No, because for every project the business case must demonstrate that the financial benefits exceed the costs, otherwise the project cannot be started at all.
explanation: The Ensure continued business justification principle applies to every project; for a mandatory project the justification is compliance with the legal obligation, but the business case still serves to select the most suitable option (here ERP, cloud tool or external processing) and to continuously verify that the project remains justified. Benefits need not be only financial – they may consist in avoiding penalties. The project mandate does not replace the business case; it is only a trigger for Starting up a project.

scenario: Horal Sport a.s. is migrating its e-shop iteratively and incrementally. The new ordering process was launched already in the second stage and according to the first measurements it increased the share of completed orders by 8%. The benefits management approach provides for measuring this benefit quarterly from launch. The project manager therefore included the measured benefit in the end stage report. The Executive objects that benefits are confirmed only after the project is closed.
question: Was the project manager's approach in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: Yes, because benefits that arise already during the project should be measured and confirmed continuously according to the benefits management approach.
No, because in PRINCE2 benefits are always confirmed only by the business layer in a benefits review held after the project is closed.
No, because the Senior user is responsible for measuring benefits, and the project manager therefore does not include measurement results in the end stage report.
Yes, because the end stage report replaces the benefits management approach, and all benefits are therefore reported in it.
explanation: The confirm benefits step of the business case management technique takes place both during subsequent delivery stages, once outcomes begin to bring benefits, and after the project ends. With iterative-incremental delivery, benefits often arise already during the project and should therefore be measured and reported according to the benefits management approach – for example in the end stage report when assessing the business case. Reviews after the project ends are only one of the opportunities to confirm benefits, not the only one.

scenario: Horal Sport a.s. is migrating its e-shop to a new platform. In the third stage, after 70% of the budget had been spent, the plan to sell via a large European marketplace, on which most of the benefits rested, fell through. The updated business case shows that the project's remaining costs will exceed the expected benefits. The Project Board nevertheless decided to continue unchanged, justifying this by the fact that most of the money has already been spent.
question: Was the Project Board's decision appropriate, and why?
options: No, because what matters is the ratio of remaining costs to expected benefits; a project without justification should be changed or closed prematurely.
Yes, because once most of the budget has been spent the project must be completed, so that the investment already made does not have to be written off entirely as a loss.
Yes, because benefits are decided by the business layer and the Project Board is responsible only for delivering products within the set tolerances.
No, because the project manager should have closed the project on their own as soon as they found that the remaining costs would exceed the project's expected benefits.
explanation: Ensure continued business justification means that the project continues only as long as the remaining investment makes sense given the expected benefits and risks; money already spent cannot be recovered and should therefore not influence the decision. If the justification ceases to exist, the project should be changed (e.g. its scope) or closed prematurely, if necessary after consulting the business layer. The PM cannot close the project alone – the decision on premature closure is made by the Project Board.

scenario: The council of the town of Valdov approved the Citizen Portal project with a budget of CZK 9 million. To save money, it proposes that the head of the IT department, Petr Dvorak, be both Executive and project manager in the project. The IT department will provide hosting and operation of the portal in the project, and development will be delivered by the external company SoftCity.
question: Is this assignment of roles appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the Executive role cannot be combined with the project manager role; direction would thus merge with day-to-day management.
Yes, because in smaller projects roles can be combined freely, provided the combination is approved by the business layer and explicitly stated in the PID.
No, because the Executive must always come from the supplier side, which bears the main responsibility for delivering products in the project.
Yes, provided that project assurance on behalf of the Executive is taken over by the project manager's deputy, who will thus ensure an independent view of the whole project.
explanation: The Executive is the single point of accountability for the project at the direction level, while the project manager manages the project day to day within the tolerances set by the Project Board; these roles cannot be merged, otherwise management by exception between the levels would cease to exist. Roles can be combined only where no conflict arises, and project assurance must be independent of the PM, so it cannot be performed by the PM's deputy. Moreover, the head of the IT department represents the internal supplier and is therefore better suited to the Senior supplier role.

scenario: The reconstruction of the internal medicine pavilion at Horni Polna Hospital is co-financed by the region as the owner of the hospital. Both the hospital's deputy director for economics and investment and the head of the investment department of the regional office want to hold the Executive role in the project. The project manager therefore proposes that the Project Board have two equal Executives who will decide jointly.
question: Is the project manager's proposal appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the project has exactly one Executive as the single point of accountability; the other party's interests must therefore be safeguarded in another way.
Yes, because with co-financing the Project Board may have several Executives, each of whom is responsible for their part of the project budget.
Yes, because the Project Board decides by voting and two equal Executives will ensure a balance between the interests of the hospital and the region.
No, because the Executive is appointed by the project manager, who will choose the person who bears the larger share of the project budget.
explanation: In PRINCE2 there is always only one Executive – the single point of accountability for the project, and this accountability cannot be divided. The Project Board is not a democratic body: the Executive decides, supported by the Senior user and Senior supplier. The region's interests can be safeguarded in other ways, e.g. by the region, as part of the business layer, setting the project's tolerances and its representative performing business assurance; moreover, the Executive is appointed by the business layer, not by the project manager.

scenario: The town of Valdov is putting together the Project Board for the Citizen Portal project. Available are: Lucie Mala, head of the transport department, whose officials will process applications from the portal; Petr Dvorak, head of the IT department, who will provide hosting; Tomas Benes, sales director of the supplier SoftCity; and Eva Simkova, the town's internal auditor. The Executive is the secretary of the town hall.
question: Who is the most suitable for the Senior user role?
options: Lucie Mala, because she represents the future users of the project's results and can specify requirements and expected benefits on their behalf.
Petr Dvorak, because the IT department will operate the portal after launch, and is therefore both its main user and supplier.
Eva Simkova, because as an internal auditor she is independent of the project and can objectively assess the requirements of all portal users.
Tomas Benes, because as the supplier's sales director he knows the portal's functions best and knows what users can expect from the system.
explanation: The Senior user represents those who will use the project's products, is responsible for how their requirements are captured, specifies the benefits and is responsible for achieving them – this is best fulfilled by the head of the transport department. The head of the IT department primarily represents the supplier side (hosting) and is therefore better suited to the Senior supplier role, as is the SoftCity representative. The internal auditor can perform project assurance, but cannot represent users.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: business layer, Project Board with three roles, Project manager and Team manager with the roles of project assurance, change authority and project support.

scenario: The Citizen Portal of the town of Valdov is being developed under a contract by the external company SoftCity. The town's IT department provides servers, security and connection to existing departmental systems. The Executive proposes that the Senior supplier role be held only by the head of the IT department, because in his view the external company has no place on the town's Project Board and the relationship with it is governed by the contract.
question: Which solution for the Senior supplier role is the most appropriate?
options: Appoint two Senior suppliers – a representative of SoftCity's management and the head of the IT department, because both supply products and resources.
Keep only the head of the IT department, because in PRINCE2 an external supplier is governed only by the contract and does not sit on the Project Board.
Appoint the SoftCity development team leader, because they create the products themselves and are therefore the most directly responsible for their quality.
Assign the Senior supplier role to the Executive, because the Executive signs the contract with the supplier and is personally responsible for the fulfilment of deliveries.
explanation: The Senior supplier represents the interests of those who design, develop and deliver the project's products; suppliers may be internal or external and there may be several Senior suppliers. An external supplier of key products should therefore have a representative on the Project Board with the authority to commit their resources, alongside the head of the IT department for internal deliveries; moreover, the contractual relationship is described in the commercial management approach. The development team leader is responsible for delivering work packages and therefore belongs in the Team manager role.

scenario: The project office of the town hall of Valdov keeps the registers in the project log for the Citizen Portal project, prepares inputs for highlight reports and organises the project manager's meetings. The Senior user role is held by the head of the transport department, who has little time for ongoing scrutiny of the project. The project manager proposed that the same project office should additionally provide user assurance on behalf of the Senior user, because it knows the project well and stands organisationally outside the project team.
question: Is this proposal appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the office here performs the project support role for the PM, and project assurance must be independent of the project manager.
Yes, because the project office stands organisationally outside the project team and is therefore sufficiently independent to perform project assurance.
Yes, because project assurance is the project manager's responsibility, which they may delegate to project support or other units.
No, because user assurance may be performed exclusively by the Senior user personally and this activity cannot be entrusted to any other person or unit.
explanation: Project assurance is performed by Project Board members for their area (business, user and supplier assurance) and they may entrust it to other persons, who must however be independent of the project manager. A project office that keeps registers and prepares reports for the PM performs the project support role and therefore cannot at the same time independently scrutinise the PM's work. The Senior user may delegate user assurance, but not to project support.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: business layer, Project Board with three roles, Project manager and Team manager with the roles of project assurance, change authority and project support.

scenario: The Executive of the Citizen Portal project, the town hall secretary Jana Novotna, does not have the capacity to continuously scrutinise on her own whether the project delivers value for money and whether the business case remains viable. She therefore tasked the town's internal auditor Eva Simkova with performing business assurance on her behalf. The auditor is not a member of the project team or of the project office.
question: Is this assignment appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because a Project Board member may entrust assurance to an independent person, but responsibility for business assurance always remains with the Executive.
Yes, because by tasking the auditor, responsibility for business assurance passes fully from the Executive to her and the Executive no longer deals with it.
No, because internal audit belongs to the business layer and must not take part in any activities within the project or in any oversight of it.
No, because business assurance must be performed by the project office, which has the best overview of the project and keeps its registers.
explanation: Project Board members are responsible for project assurance in their area and may entrust it to other persons who are independent of the project manager – the internal auditor meets this condition and is able to assess value for money and the viability of the business case. Responsibility for business assurance, however, remains with the Executive; the auditor performs it on their behalf.
