A project office providing project support, by contrast, would not be independent.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: business layer, Project Board with three roles, Project manager and Team manager with the roles of project assurance, change authority and project support.

scenario: In the Horal Sport a.s. e-shop migration project, a number of minor change requests arrive during delivery, e.g. changes to texts, colours or the order of fields in forms. The Project Board does not want to discuss each of them at its meeting. It therefore proposes to authorise the project manager to decide on change requests up to CZK 30,000 per change, with a change budget of CZK 300,000 per stage, and to record the rules in the issue management approach.
question: Is this proposal in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: Yes, because the Project Board may entrust the change authority role for minor changes to the PM as well, within clear limits and with a change budget.
No, because the change authority is always the Project Board and every change request is decided by its formal meeting.
No, because the project manager must never decide on changes, otherwise they would lose the independence needed to assess them.
Yes, because the project manager is automatically the change authority for all changes that fit within the tolerances of the current stage.
explanation: If the Project Board does not delegate the authority, it is the change authority itself; however, it may entrust it to another person or group – for minor changes also to the project manager – within clearly set limits and with a change budget. The rules of delegation are described in the issue management approach. The PM, however, is not the change authority automatically: they may decide on changes only to the extent that the Project Board explicitly entrusts to them.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: business layer, Project Board with three roles, Project manager and Team manager with the roles of project assurance, change authority and project support.

scenario: The ESG reporting project of Moravske Strojirny is managed internally; the team consists of four analysts and two developers from IT. The project manager proposes that no Team manager be appointed for the data integration work package and that they manage the work directly. They will also keep the registers in the project log and the inputs for meetings themselves, because the company has no project office.
question: Is this proposal appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because the Team manager role is optional and the project manager may manage the team directly and run project support themselves.
No, because the Team manager role is mandatory and in every work package it must be held by a person other than the project manager.
No, because project support is always provided by an organisational unit outside the project, ideally the company's permanent project office.
Yes, because in addition to these roles the project manager may also perform project assurance on behalf of the Senior user and Senior supplier.
explanation: The Team manager role in PRINCE2 is optional – if none is appointed, the project manager manages the team's work directly. Project support is by default the PM's responsibility and may be delegated (e.g. to a project office), but this is not necessary. The PM, however, must not perform project assurance, because it must be independent of them.

image.alt: PRINCE2 7 organisation chart: business layer, Project Board with three roles, Project manager and Team manager with the roles of project assurance, change authority and project support.

scenario: The board of Horni Polna Hospital appointed the deputy director for economics and investment as Executive of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction project and handed over the project mandate. The Executive then set the tolerances for the whole project in the PID on their own: cost +5% and time +2 months. The board did not decide on the tolerances and does not want to be informed if they are exceeded.
question: Is this procedure in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: No, because project tolerances are set by the business layer, which also decides if they are forecast to be exceeded; the Project Board sets only stage tolerances.
Yes, because the Executive is the single point of accountability for the project, and therefore sets the tolerances at all levels of project management on their own.
Yes, because project tolerances are proposed by the project manager and the Executive confirms them when authorising the project and each stage plan.
No, because cost and time tolerances are set by the Senior supplier, who is responsible for the estimates of work and resources of the whole supplier side.
explanation: According to Manage by exception, the business layer (here the board) sets the tolerances of the whole project and decides when they are forecast to be exceeded; within them the Project Board sets stage tolerances and the PM sets work package tolerances. The Executive is the single point of accountability in the project, but does not determine the project tolerances themselves – they are the limits of the authority delegated to them by the higher level. Without them the board would lose control over the project.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: In the second stage of the Moravske Strojirny ESG reporting project, the head of controlling, who holds the Senior user role in the project, leaves for another position outside the company. Her place is taken by a new head of controlling who is not familiar with the project. The project manager is considering how to reflect this change in the project.
question: Which course of action is the most appropriate according to PRINCE2?
options: Manage it as a change to the project ecosystem: fill the role, update the team structure and role description, and bring the new member up to speed on the project.
Leave the role vacant until the next stage boundary, when the composition of the Project Board can be changed in the Managing a stage boundary process.
Take over the Senior user role personally until the next stage boundary as the team member who knows the users' requirements best.
Record the change only in the PM's daily log, because personnel changes do not affect any approved management product or project baseline.
explanation: The organizational design and development technique also includes managing changes to the project ecosystem: when a member of the project management team leaves, the role needs to be filled again, the project management team structure and role descriptions in the PID updated and the new member brought into the project, including building relationships. The Senior user role must not remain vacant and the PM cannot take it over, because they are not a Project Board member and do not represent user interests. The PID is a baseline, so the change cannot be handled merely by an entry in the daily log.

scenario: At a Project Board meeting of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction project it emerged that the construction contractor had proposed cheaper air-conditioning whose technical solution nobody has yet verified. The director of the construction company, who is the Senior supplier on the Project Board, refused to discuss the technical solution and its quality. In his view, the Senior user and the hospital's independent quality assurance are responsible for quality.
question: Is the construction company director's attitude in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: No, because the Senior supplier is responsible for the quality of products delivered by the supplier and for the technical integrity of the project.
Yes, because the Senior user specifies user requirements, and is therefore solely responsible for the quality of the delivered products.
Yes, because the quality of products is guaranteed by quality assurance, which is independent of the project, and the Project Board therefore does not deal with it.
No, because the Senior supplier is the owner of the business case, and is therefore responsible for the quality and costs of the whole project.
explanation: The Senior supplier represents supplier interests and is responsible for the quality of products that the supplier delivers and for the technical integrity of the project – they must therefore comment on the technical solution of the air-conditioning. The Senior user is responsible for the correct capture of user requirements and for the products meeting their needs, but this does not replace the supplier's responsibility for quality. Quality assurance at the organisational level gives confidence in the quality management system, but does not remove responsibility from the roles in the project.

scenario: The town of Valdov concluded a contract with SoftCity: the first version of the Citizen Portal will be delivered for a fixed price and further extensions will be paid according to hours actually worked. The contract also contains penalties for delay and rules for approving additional work. In Initiating a project the project manager wants to describe how the relationship with the supplier will be managed – monitoring contract performance, evaluating the supplier's performance and the procedure in case of disputes.
question: Where does this description best belong according to PRINCE2?
options: In the commercial management approach in the PID, because it describes the management of commercial relationships with the project's suppliers.
In the work package description for the SoftCity team, because in PRINCE2 the contractual relationship is dealt with exclusively at the work package level.
In the project brief, because it remains the basic agreement between the commissioner and the supplier of the portal throughout the project.
In the issue management approach, because every change to the contract with the supplier is a request for change to the project baseline.
explanation: The commercial management approach is part of the PID and belongs to the Organizing practice; it describes how commercial relationships with suppliers will be managed in the project, i.e. the contractual and supply context. The work package description does contain the work assignment for the supplier's team, but does not replace the overall approach to the commercial relationship. The project brief is not maintained after initiation, because it is replaced by the PID.

scenario: The council of the town of Valdov issued the project mandate for the Citizen Portal. Within Starting up a project, the project manager is preparing inputs for the decision on starting initiation. In doing so they began to draw up a detailed project plan for the entire two years of the project, including a schedule of all of the supplier's sprints, so that the Project Board would have a complete overview.
question: Is this approach appropriate, and why?
options: No, because in Starting up a project only the initiation stage is planned; the project plan is prepared only in Initiating a project.
Yes, because the Project Board needs a complete and detailed project plan in order to decide on authorising project initiation.
No, because the Executive draws up the project plan alone and the project manager prepares only the stage plans of the individual stages of the project.
Yes, because the purpose of Starting up a project is to prepare the PID, which includes a detailed project plan for the whole project.
explanation: In Starting up a project the project manager prepares the project brief and the initiation stage plan; on that basis the Project Board decides whether it makes sense to invest in initiation. The project plan is created only in Initiating a project as part of the PID, when the requirements, approaches and estimates are known. A detailed schedule of all sprints for two years would, moreover, go far beyond the planning horizon.

image.alt: Plan levels in PRINCE2 7: project plan, stage plan, optional team plan and exception plan, which replaces the project plan or stage plan.

scenario: The project manager of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction at Horni Polna Hospital is preparing the project plan in Initiating a project. The construction design documentation is not yet finished and the contractor will be selected only in six months. The manager nevertheless wants to include in the project plan a detailed day-by-day schedule of all construction work for the whole 18 months, so that the Project Board sees exact dates.
question: Is this approach to planning appropriate, and why?
options: No, because detailed planning is possible only within the planning horizon; the project plan should be high-level and detail belongs in stage plans.
Yes, because the project plan must contain a detailed schedule of all work, otherwise the Project Board cannot approve it when authorising the project.
Yes, because a detailed schedule for the whole project replaces stage plans, which will then not need to be prepared at stage boundaries.
No, because the construction work schedule belongs exclusively in the contractor's team plan and is not included in the project's plans at all.
explanation: The planning horizon is the period for which it is possible to plan with reasonable accuracy; beyond it, a detailed daily schedule would be only an estimate with false precision, especially when the documentation is not yet finished and the contractor has not been selected. The project plan therefore remains high-level (main products, milestones, costs) and details are added to the stage plan for the next stage at its boundary. The contractor's optional team plan does not replace the stage plan.

image.alt: Plan levels in PRINCE2 7: project plan, stage plan, optional team plan and exception plan, which replaces the project plan or stage plan.

scenario: In Initiating a project, the team of the Moravske Strojirny ESG reporting project drew up the first version of a product breakdown structure. Under the product "ESG reporting tool" it listed the items "Plant data connectors", "Emissions calculation methodology", "Connector testing", "Meetings with plants" and "User manual". The project manager is checking the structure before further planning.
question: Which assessment of this product breakdown structure is correct?
options: Testing and meetings are activities, not products; they should be replaced by the products arising from them, e.g. a connector test report.
The structure is fine, because a product breakdown structure should contain all the products and activities that need to be delivered.
The emissions calculation methodology does not belong in the structure, because in PRINCE2 a product can only be a tangible output or finished software.
The user manual does not belong in the structure, because documents are management products and are listed in the PID.
explanation: A product breakdown structure is a hierarchical breakdown of products, not activities; work is derived from the products only later (e.g. in a work breakdown structure). The items "Connector testing" and "Meetings with plants" therefore need to be replaced by the products that result from them, e.g. a test report or an agreed schedule of data deliveries. A product can also be an intangible output or a document, so both the methodology and the user manual belong in the structure.

scenario: The ESG reporting tool of Moravske Strojirny needs energy consumption data from a new ERP module delivered by another project of the company, with a deadline in March. The ESG reporting project has no influence over the delivery of the module. The project manager is preparing the project plan.
question: How should the project manager most appropriately deal with the ERP module in the plan?
options: Capture it as an external dependency of the affected products, monitor its delivery and assess the risk, because the delivery is not within the project's influence.
Include the development of the ERP module in the scope of the ESG reporting project, so that the project manager has its deadline fully under control.
Not mention the module in the plan at all, because products that the project does not create itself are not part of its plans or its scope.
Record the module in the issue register as an issue whose delivery date is outside the control of both the project manager and the Project Board.
explanation: A dependency on a product delivered by someone outside the project is an external dependency; the plan should capture it so that it is clear which products and activities depend on it, and the project should monitor it. Because the project cannot influence the delivery, it is appropriate to assess the related risk of delay as well – risks are analysed in parallel with planning. Extending the project's scope to include someone else's product would be disproportionate, and it is not an issue that has already occurred.

scenario: In the Citizen Portal project of the town of Valdov, the SoftCity development team leader (Team manager) has taken over the work package "Parking permits module". They want to manage the work according to their own sprint plan in the tool SoftCity uses, and not according to the town's stage plan. The project manager is unsure whether PRINCE2 permits this.
question: How should this request be assessed according to PRINCE2?
options: It is acceptable, because the Team manager may create a team plan for the package in their own format agreed with the PM, in line with the work package description.
It is not acceptable, because external suppliers must work exclusively according to the stage plan and team plans are intended only for internal teams.
It is acceptable and the team plan replaces the stage plan for the duration of the work package, and the PM no longer follows the stage plan.
It is not acceptable, because the Project Board must approve every team plan at its meeting in Directing a project before work starts.
explanation: A team plan is an optional plan that the Team manager prepares for the execution of a work package; it may take the form of a sprint plan in the supplier's format, provided it is consistent with the work package description and agreed with the PM. It does not replace the stage plan, however – the PM continues to manage the stage according to the stage plan and the Team manager submits checkpoint reports to them. The Project Board does not approve team plans; it approves the project plan, stage plans and exception plans.

image.alt: Plan levels in PRINCE2 7: project plan, stage plan, optional team plan and exception plan, which replaces the project plan or stage plan.

scenario: During the reconstruction of the internal medicine pavilion, the work package "Electrical installation" slips by three weeks because of a late delivery of switchboards and thus exceeds the work package's time tolerance. The stage as a whole remains, even with the delay, within the tolerance set by the Project Board. The site manager (Team manager) therefore began preparing an exception plan for the work package and wants to submit it to the Project Board for approval.
question: Is the site manager's approach appropriate, and why?
options: No, because exception plans are not prepared for work packages; the Team manager raises an issue and the PM can take corrective action within the stage tolerance.
Yes, because every tolerance breach is dealt with by an exception plan, which is approved by the Project Board in Directing a project.
Yes, because an exception plan takes the place of the team plan for which the Team manager is responsible, and is approved by the same body as the team plan.
No, because in this case the exception plan is prepared by the project manager and submitted to the business layer for a decision on how to proceed with the project.
explanation: An exception plan is prepared only at project or stage level (it replaces the project plan or stage plan), not for a work package. When a Team manager forecasts that the work package tolerance will be exceeded, they raise an issue to the project manager; if the stage remains within tolerance, the PM can take corrective action themselves, e.g. amend the work package description. The Project Board becomes involved only when the stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.

image.alt: Plan levels in PRINCE2 7: project plan, stage plan, optional team plan and exception plan, which replaces the project plan or stage plan.

scenario: The project manager of the Citizen Portal of the town of Valdov is preparing a work package description for the SoftCity team for the work package "Online payment of fees". The portal is being developed by the external company SoftCity in two-week sprints, and payments must go through the payment gateway of the bank with which the town has a contract. The SoftCity team leader (Team manager) will take over the package in Managing product delivery.
question: Which set of items best belongs in the work package description?
options: Products and their product descriptions, time and cost tolerances, the interface to the payment gateway and the frequency of checkpoint reports.
The project's business case, an overview of the portal's expected benefits, project tolerances set by the business layer and a detailed description of the risks of the whole project.
SoftCity's internal hourly rates and margins, which govern the price calculation and invoicing of the work package under the concluded contract for work.
The complete stage plan of the stage, a breakdown of all work packages of other teams and a list of Project Board members with their contact details.
explanation: A work package description is the formal handover of responsibility for the work to the Team manager; it contains the products and their product descriptions, techniques, interfaces, work package tolerances, constraints, the frequency and form of checkpoint reports, the escalation procedure and the way products are approved. Project tolerances, benefits and the business case are information for the direction level, not for assigning work to the team. The supplier's rates and margins belong to its commercial relationship, not to the work assignment.

scenario: The project manager of the Moravske Strojirny ESG reporting project is preparing the stage plan of the second stage. They have gradually defined the products, divided the work into work packages, estimated effort and drawn up the schedule and budget. They want to carry out risk analysis only as the very last step after the plan has been documented, so as to assess the finished plan as a whole.
question: Is the chosen planning approach appropriate, and why?
options: No, because risks should be analysed in parallel with every planning step, so that they are reflected in the estimates, schedule and budget.
Yes, because risk analysis is the last step of the PRINCE2 planning technique, and is therefore carried out only after the whole plan has been documented.
No, because plan risks are analysed exclusively by project assurance and the project manager merely takes them into the plan from the project's risk register.
Yes, because risks are recorded in the risk register only after planning ends, once the Project Board approves the plan and authorises the stage.
explanation: The PRINCE2 planning technique has the steps of defining and analysing products, organising work packages, estimating, scheduling, budgeting and documenting the plan; risk analysis runs in parallel with all the steps. Each step can reveal new risks and the responses to them (e.g. additional activities or contingencies) must be reflected in the estimates, schedule and budget. Analysing risks only on the finished plan would lead to its rework or to an unrealistic plan.

scenario: The new Horal Sport a.s. e-shop must be launched no later than a week before Black Friday; moving the date would mean losing the main season. The teams work iteratively and incrementally. For the final stage the Project Board therefore set a very small time tolerance and a larger scope tolerance: requirements are ordered by priority and low-priority features can be postponed to the next release.
question: Is this way of setting tolerances appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because with iterative-incremental delivery prioritised requirements make it possible to vary scope within tolerance and hold a fixed deadline.
No, because scope must be fixed in the project product description and in PRINCE2 tolerances can be set only for time and cost.
Yes, because with iterative delivery tolerances are not used and the scope of each sprint and of the entire stage is decided solely by the development team.
No, because the scope tolerance can be set only by the business layer for the whole project, and the Project Board therefore must not set it for a stage.
explanation: Scope tolerance is one of the seven tolerances; with iterative-incremental delivery, time is typically held fixed and scope is managed by requirement priorities within an agreed tolerance. The Project Board sets stage tolerances within the project tolerances determined by the business layer, including the scope tolerance. Management by exception applies even in iterative work – if it were forecast that not even the priority features would be delivered, this is an exception to be escalated.

scenario: The project manager of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction at Horni Polna Hospital is finalising the project product description. The head nurse and the head physician of internal medicine have formulated what they expect from the new pavilion. The Senior user wants clarity on the basis on which the pavilion will be accepted at the end of the project.
question: Which entry is the most appropriate for the project product description?
options: Acceptance criterion: before patients move in, the pavilion has a positive opinion from the hygiene authority on commissioning; acceptance is confirmed by the Senior user.
Quality specification: the washable coating on the walls of the rooms must withstand at least 10,000 disinfection cycles without visible damage to the surface.
Tolerance of the Electrical installation work package: time +1 week, cost +3%; site manager's checkpoint report every Friday.
The delivery of switchboards depends on the manufacturer, who reports a possible delay; risk owner Senior supplier, chosen response reduce the threat.
explanation: The project product description describes the project's main product, users' quality expectations, acceptance criteria and the method and responsibilities for acceptance – a measurable criterion that specifies who confirms acceptance therefore belongs here. The quality specification of an individual coating belongs in the product description of a component product. Work package tolerances are stated in the work package description and the threat of delay in the risk register.

scenario: Horni Polna Hospital set itself the goal of reducing the carbon footprint of its investments. When preparing the stage plan for the construction stage, the project manager of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction therefore also took into account how the building will be built: sorting and recycling of construction waste, consolidation of material deliveries and reduction of transport to the construction site. The construction company's director (Senior supplier) objects that sustainability concerns only the properties of the finished pavilion, not the way it is built.
question: Is the project manager's approach in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: Yes, because planning in PRINCE2 7 also takes into account the sustainability of the way products are delivered, not just the sustainability of the finished products.
No, because in PRINCE2 sustainability is addressed only in the business case and the sustainability management approach and is not reflected in stage plans.
No, because the way of building is decided exclusively by the contractor under the contract for work and the project manager should not interfere with it in any way.
Yes, because in PRINCE2 7 sustainability takes precedence over all other performance targets, including cost and time.
explanation: In the Plans practice PRINCE2 7 introduces the concept of delivery sustainability – the sustainability of the way products are delivered, not just the sustainability of the products themselves. A stage plan can and should therefore include measures such as waste sorting or reduced transport, so that the project meets its sustainability objectives. Sustainability is one of the seven performance targets and is balanced against the others; it does not automatically take precedence over cost or time.

scenario: A regional hospital is preparing a project to reconstruct the internal medicine pavilion. Project manager Jana Kralova (Project manager) is drawing up the project product description in the Starting up a project process. Head nurse Lucie Vavrova, who represents users on the Project Board as Senior user, requires that "the new rooms be quiet and pleasant for patients and that staff can move around in them easily". Kralova entered this sentence in the project product description as one of the acceptance criteria.
question: Is this entry appropriate among the acceptance criteria, and why?
options: No, because it is a user quality expectation; acceptance criteria must be measurable and prioritised, e.g. night-time room noise up to 35 dB.
Yes, because acceptance criteria should capture users' expectations in their own words and the measurable values will be added later by the Team manager.
Yes, because the requirement was formulated by the Senior user, so nobody else needs to clarify or prioritise the acceptance criteria.
No, because in PRINCE2 7 acceptance criteria are not stated in the project product description but in the product descriptions of component products.
explanation: The sentence describes the expected quality in general terms and therefore belongs in the project product description as a user quality expectation. Acceptance criteria are measurable and prioritised criteria derived from it (e.g. noise level in dB or door width for a bed), on the basis of which users accept the project product. The option about product descriptions is wrong: acceptance criteria are part of the project product description, whereas product descriptions contain the quality specifications of individual products.

scenario: A logistics company is introducing a new warehouse management system (WMS) at a distribution centre near Brno, which an external supplier is developing in two-week sprints. Project manager Eva Markova (Project manager) is preparing, with representatives of the warehouse and the supplier, the product description for the product "Picking module". For the quality specifications section she proposed to enter: "The response of the handheld scanner to confirming a warehouse location is at most 1 second for 95% of operations with 150 warehouse workers working concurrently." As the quality method she stated a load test.
question: Is this entry in the product description appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because quality specifications state the measurable levels that the finished product must reach and against which quality control is carried out.
Yes, because such precise values replace the acceptance criteria in the project product description, which then no longer needs to be maintained.
No, because measurable performance values belong exclusively in the acceptance criteria in the project product description, not with component products.
No, because the quality specifications of products are set by the company's quality assurance unit, not by the project team with users.
explanation: A product description should state for each product the quality specifications – measurable criteria and levels against which quality control verifies that the product conforms – together with the quality method. The acceptance criteria in the project product description concern the project product as a whole and are not replaced by component quality specifications – the two complement each other. Quality assurance is an independent function of the organisation that gives assurance that quality is managed correctly, but it does not write the specifications of individual products.

scenario: In the project to reconstruct the internal medicine pavilion of a regional hospital, an inspection of the new electrical installation on the second floor was carried out according to the stage plan. The inspection technician found no defects and the hospital's technical deputy director Marek Hron, whom the product description names as approver, approved the product. A project support officer asks project manager Jana Kralova where to record both facts.
question: How should these facts be recorded?
options: The inspection carried out and its result in the quality register, the product status "approved" in the product register; both are part of the project log.
Both the inspection and the approval in the quality register, because in PRINCE2 7 the product register is kept only for products handed over into operation at the end of the project.
The inspection result in the Project manager's daily log and the product approval in the issue register as a resolved issue with no need for a further decision.
The inspection in the configuration item record of the electrical installation and the approval in the product status account, which is stored as part of the PID.
explanation: The quality register records planned and performed quality control activities and their results, while the product register tracks the project's products, their status and acceptance; in PRINCE2 7 both belong in the project log. Configuration item record and product status account are terms from the 6th edition, which the product register replaced. Moreover, the product register is kept for all of the project's products, not just those handed over at the end.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records from the daily log to the product register.

scenario: A statutory city is carrying out the Citizen Portal project within the Digital City programme. The town hall's quality department, which does not work on the project in any way, checks once a year whether the city's projects comply with the approved methodology and quality standards. Petra Stastna, head of the citizen services department, who is on the Project Board as Senior user, has also tasked an experienced clerk from her department with continuously verifying, on her behalf, whether user requirements are correctly reflected in the portal's products.
question: Which statement correctly describes these two activities?
options: The quality department's check is quality assurance, because it is independent of the project; the clerk's work is project assurance on behalf of the Senior user.
Both activities are project assurance, because both give the Project Board assurance that the project is managed correctly and according to the city's methodology.
The quality department's check is project assurance on behalf of the Executive; the clerk's work, checking the portal's products, is quality control.
Both activities are quality assurance, because neither the quality department nor the clerk are Project Board members and neither creates products themselves.
explanation: Quality assurance is a planned and systematic activity of the organisation, independent of the project team, which gives assurance that projects and their products will meet the required standards – this corresponds to the quality department's check. Project assurance is the responsibility of Project Board members for their area; the Senior user may entrust user assurance to a delegated person, such as the clerk here. The claim that both activities are project assurance confuses an independent function of the organisation with oversight performed on behalf of the steering board.

scenario: In the new warehouse system project of the logistics company, the product description of the "Goods receipt" module sets as the quality method a verification test with key warehouse users; the approver is the shift supervisor. The supplier's Team manager Filip Urban found that the team is falling behind. He therefore proposes to skip the test with users and replace it with an internal code review, which the team can complete within the sprint. He claims that as Team manager he can adjust the way quality is checked himself.
question: How should the Team manager proceed?
options: Pass an issue (request for change) to the Project manager, because the quality method is part of the approved product description.
Replace the test with the code review and record the result in the quality register, because the choice of quality method is within the Team manager's authority.
Send the Project Board an exception report, because changing the quality method constitutes a breach of the work package's quality tolerance.
Agree with the shift supervisor as approver that they will approve the module even without the test, and state this in the next checkpoint report.
explanation: The quality method is part of the product description, which as an approved management product is under change control. The Team manager cannot change it on their own; they can propose a change, which the Project manager captures as an issue (request for change) and passes for decision to whoever has the delegated authority. A Team manager never submits an exception report – even a forecast breach of work package tolerances is escalated to the Project manager as an issue.

scenario: A construction company has completed all construction work in the internal medicine pavilion of a regional hospital. The company's director Ales Pokorny, who is on the Project Board as Senior supplier, announced that the company carried out all of its internal checks and tests without defects, and that the project product is therefore accepted. The project product description contains acceptance criteria (e.g. noise level, hygiene limits, capacity of bed lifts) and as the acceptance method a two-week trial operation with nurses and doctors under the direction of the Senior user.
question: Is the Senior supplier's claim about acceptance of the product correct, and why?
options: No, because acceptance takes place according to the acceptance method and responsibilities in the project product description, i.e. only once the acceptance criteria have been verified by users.
Yes, because the Senior supplier is responsible for the quality of the supplier's products and their confirmation of test results replaces acceptance of the product by users.
Yes, because successful tests are recorded in the quality register, and the product is thereby automatically accepted and shown in the product register as accepted.
No, because in PRINCE2 7 acceptance of the project product is decided exclusively by the Executive on the recommendation of the quality assurance unit.
explanation: The project product description sets out the acceptance criteria, the acceptance method and the responsibilities for acceptance; here it is a trial operation with users led by the Senior user. The supplier's internal tests are part of quality control, but they do not replace acceptance of the project product by users. The Senior supplier is indeed responsible for the quality of the supplier's products, but acceptance is carried out by those designated for it in the project product description.

scenario: In the Citizen Portal project of a statutory city, the head of the citizen services department, in the Senior user role, entered 24 acceptance criteria in the draft project product description and marked all of them as mandatory. The Senior supplier pointed out that meeting all the criteria by the planned launch would significantly raise costs beyond what the business case allows for. Project manager Tomas Bures is to finish the project product description as part of the project brief.
question: Which action should the Project manager take?
options: Go through the acceptance criteria with users and set their priorities, so that quality can be balanced against cost and time in the business case.
Keep all criteria mandatory and record the risk of cost overrun in the risk register with the response accept and Senior user as owner.
Strike out the criteria that the Senior supplier marks as the most expensive, because the supplier decides the level of quality according to their capacity.
Move the acceptance criteria into the product descriptions of individual products, where the Team manager can modify them during delivery.
explanation: Acceptance criteria in PRINCE2 are measurable and prioritised criteria; priorities make it possible to decide on trade-offs between quality, cost and time so that the project remains justified. The Senior user specifies the criteria, but their consistency with the business case, which the Executive owns, is assessed by the Project Board. Keeping everything mandatory and merely recording a risk does not solve the problem – a cost overrun is almost certain in that case and the conflict is only postponed.

scenario: An external supplier is delivering the logistics company's new warehouse system iteratively and incrementally in two-week sprints within management stages. Distribution centre manager Hana Kopecka, in the Senior user role, wants to refine the priorities of requirements during the stages based on warehouse workers' experience with the first modules. Project manager Eva Markova is preparing the quality management approach and is considering how to plan and control quality in the project.
question: Which setting of the approach to quality is appropriate for this project?
options: Refine requirements continuously under change control and check each increment against its product description, so that defects are detected early.
Fix all quality specifications already in the initiation stage and verify quality with a single acceptance test of the whole system shortly before launch.
Not create product descriptions for iterative delivery and leave quality to the supplier's judgement, because requirements will change anyway.
Postpone the refinement of requirements to the last stage, not change priorities during the stages until then, and stick to the original assignment.
explanation: PRINCE2 7 allows for requirements to be refined continuously, but always under change control, and for quality to be verified continuously rather than only by a final test. With iterative delivery, each increment therefore undergoes quality control against the quality specifications in its product description. Fixing all specifications at the start corresponds more to a linear-sequential approach and here it would prevent making use of warehouse workers' feedback.

scenario: In the project to reconstruct the internal medicine pavilion, the product description of the product "Medical gas pipework" sets as the quality method a pressure test and a documentation check. The approver is the hospital's technical deputy director. Site manager Petr Holub, in the Team manager role, proposed that the reviewer role in this check be performed by the technician who installed the pipework himself, because he knows the installation best.
question: Is the Team manager's proposal appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the reviewer should assess the product independently of its creator (producer), against the quality specifications in the product description.
Yes, because the independence of the check is ensured only by the approver and the reviewer may also be the person who created the product and knows it best.
Yes, because the division of roles in a quality check is decided by the Team manager alone and it is enough to record the change in the quality register for the relevant check.
No, because the reviewer must always be a project assurance member appointed by the Project Board, never an employee of the supplier company.
explanation: The product description sets out responsibilities for quality: the producer creates the product, the reviewer assesses it independently against the quality specifications and the approver confirms that the product is complete and fit for purpose. If the review were carried out by the installer himself, the check would lose its independence. The approver does not replace independent assessment but confirms the product only on the basis of it; PRINCE2 does not require that the reviewer always come from project assurance.

scenario: A logistics company has a certified quality management system under ISO 9001 with its own directives for testing and accepting IT systems. The external supplier of the warehouse system uses its own testing methodology. In the initiation stage, project manager Eva Markova is preparing the quality management approach as part of the project initiation documentation (PID).
question: What should the quality management approach contain in this project?
options: How the company's directives and the supplier's procedures will be applied – techniques, standards and responsibilities for meeting the quality specifications and acceptance criteria.
A complete overview of all planned and performed quality checks with their results, which the Project manager updates after each sprint.
The product descriptions of all products including quality specifications, so that the PID contains all quality information in one place.
A copy of the entire company ISO 9001 manual, because the quality management approach must not specify or tailor the organisation's standards in the project in any way.
explanation: The quality management approach in the PID describes how quality will be achieved in the project: which techniques, standards, roles and responsibilities will be used to meet the quality specifications and acceptance criteria, including how the company's and the supplier's standards will be applied. The overview of planned and performed checks belongs in the quality register in the project log. Product descriptions are separate management products, which the quality management approach does not replace.

scenario: A logistics company is introducing a new warehouse system that must be launched by the end of October, i.e. before the pre-Christmas season. The handheld barcode scanners will be supplied by a company that has so far carried out only small orders and has no experience with delivering 200 units. Project manager Eva Markova is entering a new risk in the risk register and wants to formulate its description according to the recommended structure.
question: Which risk description is the most appropriate for the risk register?
options: Because the scanner supplier has no experience with such a large delivery, the scanners may be delivered after September, which would push the system launch into the season.
The scanner supplier has no experience with delivering 200 units and has so far carried out only small orders, which poses a serious risk to the new warehouse system.
The launch of the warehouse system may slip into the pre-Christmas season, which would mean higher overtime costs and the loss of some orders.
The barcode scanners were delivered three weeks later than the contract specified, and the system launch will therefore slip into the pre-Christmas season.
explanation: A good risk description separates the cause (a known fact – an inexperienced supplier), the uncertain event (late delivery of the scanners) and its impact on objectives (launch slipping into the season). The description of the supplier's inexperience states only the cause without an uncertain event, and the description of the launch slipping captures only the impact without a cause and event. The description of an actual delivery delay is no longer a risk but an issue, because the event has occurred.

scenario: In the project to reconstruct the internal medicine pavilion there is a threat that Legionella bacteria will multiply in the new water pipework after filling, which would delay the opening of the ward. Project manager Jana Kralova entered in the risk register as risk owner the hospital's technical deputy director, who will monitor the risk and oversee that responses are carried out and are effective. As risk action owner she named the construction company's plumber, who will carry out thermal disinfection and arrange sampling.
question: Is this entry in the risk register appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because the risk owner manages the risk and oversees the responses, whereas the risk action owner carries out specific agreed actions.
Yes, because the risk owner must always be a member of the management of the user organisation and the risk action owner always an employee of the supplier.
No, because the risk owner of all risks should be the Project manager, who keeps the risk register and is responsible for managing risks in the stage.
No, because the risk owner and the risk action owner must be the same person, otherwise responsibility for the response to the risk would not be unambiguous.
explanation: The risk owner is the person responsible for managing a specific risk – they monitor it and oversee that the chosen responses are carried out and are effective; this corresponds to the role of the technical deputy director. The risk action owner (risk actionee in the 6th edition) carries out specific agreed actions, here disinfection and sampling. The notion that the risk owner is always the Project manager is wrong: the PM keeps the risk register, but the risk owner should be whoever is best able to manage the given risk.

image.alt: Overview of risk responses in PRINCE2 7 for threats and opportunities and the difference between risk owner and risk action owner.

scenario: A regional hospital is concluding a contract with a construction company for the reconstruction of the internal medicine pavilion. Construction material prices fluctuate sharply and there is a threat that construction costs will exceed the budget. The project Executive, hospital director Tomas Broz, pushed through a contract clause under which both savings and any cost overrun against the target price are split between the hospital and the construction company in a 50:50 ratio.
question: What type of risk response according to PRINCE2 7 is this?
options: Share – the hospital and the construction company share both the negative and the positive deviation from the target price.
Transfer – the financial impact of the threat is shifted entirely, by contract, to the construction company as a third party.
Reduce – the clause lowers the probability that construction material prices will rise during construction.
Accept – the hospital consciously takes no action and merely monitors the development of material prices.
explanation: With the share response, the organisation shares both losses and gains with a partner – here the overrun and the savings against the target price. Transfer would mean shifting the financial impact of the threat to a third party (e.g. through insurance or a fixed price), which does not apply here, because the hospital continues to bear half of the overrun. The clause does not change the probability of price rises in any way, so it is not reduce either.

image.alt: Overview of risk responses in PRINCE2 7 for threats and opportunities and the difference between risk owner and risk action owner.

scenario: A statutory city's Citizen Portal is to allow login through the national electronic identification system. Its administrator is preparing a major update for the portal's launch date, so there is a threat that the interface will not be available on launch day. The project team prepared a fallback login through a data mailbox, which is activated only if the interface does not work at launch. Part of the risk budget is set aside for its possible deployment.
question: What type of risk response is this?
options: Prepare contingent plans – the actions are carried out only if the risk event occurs, and they mitigate its impact.
Reduce – the fallback login lowers the probability that the national system's interface will be unavailable.
Avoid – the prepared solution completely removes the uncertainty about whether citizens will be able to use the portal after launch.
Transfer – the impact of a possible outage will be borne by the administrator of the national system, who is responsible for the interface's availability.
explanation: A contingent plan is prepared in advance but is triggered only when the event occurs; it does not change the probability of an outage, only mitigates its impact, and is typically funded from the risk budget. A reduce response would have to influence whether the national system's interface is available, which the fallback login does not do. Avoid would require removing the uncertainty itself, e.g. by the portal not depending on the interface at all at launch.

image.alt: Overview of risk responses in PRINCE2 7 for threats and opportunities and the difference between risk owner and risk action owner.

scenario: The supplier of the logistics company's new warehouse system said it could complete the integration with the transport system a month earlier if its developers have experienced users available to test the interface quickly. Earlier integration would save the company part of the cost of running the old and new systems in parallel. Distribution centre manager Hana Kopecka, in the Senior user role, therefore released two experienced dispatchers full-time for two months. It still remains uncertain whether the supplier will actually shorten the deadline.
question: How should this response be recorded in the risk register?
options: As an enhance response, because the measure increases the probability of the favourable event but does not remove the uncertainty.
As an exploit response, because the project actively commits resources to make the favourable event actually happen.
As a reject response, because apart from releasing the dispatchers the project takes no further measures to exploit the opportunity.
As a share response, because both the company and the supplier contribute their own people and time to exploiting the opportunity.
explanation: Enhance changes the probability or impact of an opportunity in its favour – here the chance of earlier completion is increased, but the result remains uncertain. Exploit would mean removing the uncertainty entirely and ensuring that the opportunity occurs, which releasing the dispatchers does not guarantee. The reject response comes from the 6th edition and is not among the PRINCE2 7 responses; share would require an agreement with a partner on sharing gains and losses.

image.alt: Overview of risk responses in PRINCE2 7 for threats and opportunities and the difference between risk owner and risk action owner.

scenario: In the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction project there is a threat that the delivery of decorative light fittings for the waiting room will be delayed. The fittings can also be installed after the ward opens and an expedited delivery from another manufacturer would cost more than the possible delay, so the risk owner chose the accept response. Project manager Jana Kralova left the risk in the risk register and at each stage status assessment checks whether its probability or impact has changed. The Senior supplier proposes removing accepted risks from the register to make it clearer.
question: Is the project manager's approach appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because accept means consciously not acting now but continuing to monitor the risk in case its probability or impact changes.
Yes, because for threats accept is only a temporary response, which must be replaced by a reduce or avoid response by the end of the stage.
No, because there is nothing left to manage for an accepted risk and the risk register should contain only risks for which planned actions are under way.
No, because the accept response is not permissible for threats in PRINCE2 7 and the risk should have been dealt with by one of the active responses.
explanation: Accept is a conscious decision not to take any steps now, typically because they would cost more than the possible impact; the risk, however, remains in the risk register and continues to be monitored in case the situation changes. The risk register records all identified risks with their status and history, not just those with actions under way, so the Senior supplier's proposal is not appropriate. In PRINCE2 7 accept is a permissible response to both threats and opportunities and has no time limit.

image.alt: Overview of risk responses in PRINCE2 7 for threats and opportunities and the difference between risk owner and risk action owner.

scenario: The Citizen Portal project is part of the city's Digital City programme. The programme steering board, which represents the business layer for the project, stated that the city is willing to take only very small risks related to leakage of citizens' personal data, whereas for risks of delay to less important features it is willing to risk more. At the same time it set that the aggregate expected value of threats to the project's cost must not exceed CZK 1.2 million.
question: Which statement classifies these directions correctly?
options: The attitude to data leaks and to delays is risk appetite; the CZK 1.2 million limit is risk tolerance, whose forecast breach is an exception.
The attitude to data leaks and to delays is risk tolerance; the CZK 1.2 million limit is risk appetite, i.e. a boundary that the project must not exceed under any circumstances.
The attitude to data leaks and to delays is risk appetite; the CZK 1.2 million limit is a risk budget, from which the project pays for responses to threats.
Both represent the project's risk exposure, which the programme steering board set as the baseline for assessing all risks.
explanation: Risk appetite expresses how much and what kind of risk the organisation is willing to take – here a different attitude to data leaks and to delays. Risk tolerance is a measurable threshold of acceptable outcomes for a given objective in its units (here CZK 1.2 million for cost); a forecast breach of it means an exception and escalation. A risk budget, by contrast, is an amount set aside to fund responses to risks, not a limit on aggregate exposure.

scenario: In the second stage of the logistics company's new warehouse system project, project manager Eva Markova carried out a regular risk review. Because of newly identified threats in the integration with the transport system, the aggregate risk exposure of the stage now exceeds the risk tolerance that the Project Board set for the stage. The forecasts for time, cost and scope of the stage are so far within tolerance.
question: Which action should the project manager take?
options: Prepare an exception report for the Project Board, because a breach of the stage's risk tolerance is forecast even though the other targets are within tolerance.
Record the new threats in the risk register and inform the Project Board in the next highlight report, because the stage's time, cost and scope are within tolerance.
Move funds from the change budget to the risk budget and start responses to the new threats, because the project manager decides on stage risks alone.
Ask the supplier's Team manager for an exception report, because the new threats arose in their work package and their team should deal with them.
explanation: Risk is one of the seven performance targets with its own tolerance; a forecast that the aggregate risk exposure of the stage will exceed the tolerance set by the Project Board is an exception and the Project manager must escalate it with an exception report. Waiting for the regular highlight report is not enough, because outside tolerances the Project manager has no authority to continue. Moreover, an exception report is never submitted by a Team manager – they escalate to the Project manager in the form of an issue.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: During the reconstruction of the internal medicine pavilion of a regional hospital, the power supply of the neighbouring intensive care unit is to be switched over to a new switchboard in March. If the backup power source failed during the switchover, it would endanger patients on life-support equipment within minutes. Project manager Jana Kralova is assessing the risk and recording its characteristics in the risk register.
question: Which assessment uses the terms proximity and velocity correctly?
options: Proximity: the risk can occur only at the switchover in March. Velocity: very high, the impact appears within minutes.
Proximity: very high, the impact appears within minutes. Velocity: the risk can occur only at the switchover in March.
Proximity: high, because an outage would have a serious impact on patients. Velocity: low, it is a one-off action.
Proximity: the risk can occur only at the switchover in March. Velocity: low, because a failure of the power source is unlikely.
explanation: Proximity expresses when the risk event may occur (here at the March switchover), whereas velocity, which PRINCE2 7 newly emphasises, describes how quickly the impact appears after the event occurs (here within minutes). The assessment that swaps the two terms is therefore wrong. The assessment with low velocity correctly determines proximity but confuses velocity with the probability of occurrence.

scenario: The Citizen Portal project budget contains a risk budget of CZK 400,000 for contingent plans and other risk responses. The Project Board also set a change budget of CZK 300,000, whose use is decided by the head of the citizen services department as change authority; it is already almost exhausted. The head of the department is now asking for a new form for booking appointments at the office to be added to the portal. Project manager Tomas Bures is considering paying for the form from the as yet unused risk budget.
question: Is such a use of the risk budget appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the risk budget serves only to fund risk responses, whereas the form, as a change, is decided by the change authority or the board.
No, because use of both the risk budget and the change budget is decided exclusively by the business layer and neither the Project Board nor the PM can interfere with them.
Yes, because both the risk budget and the change budget are part of the stage budget and the Project manager can move funds between them as needed.
Yes, because the new form will reduce the risk of citizen dissatisfaction with the portal, and it is therefore a reduce response paid from the risk budget.
explanation: The risk budget is set aside for risk responses, typically contingent plans, whereas the change budget serves to fund approved changes to the baseline. The new form is a request for change: it is decided by the change authority within the limits of the change budget, and if that is not sufficient, the issue must be escalated to the Project Board. Retrospectively labelling a change as a risk response would circumvent the authorities that the Project Board delegated for deciding on changes.

scenario: The risk register of the new warehouse system project contains a risk that the supplier's key developer, the only one with knowledge of the interface to the transport system, will leave the company. A continuous transfer of knowledge to a second developer was planned as the response. This week the developer actually handed in their notice and leaves in two weeks, while the knowledge transfer is only partly complete. The supplier's Team manager Filip Urban informed project manager Eva Markova of this.
question: How should the project manager deal with this situation?
options: Deal with it as an issue using the issue management procedure, because the risk has already occurred, and record this in the risk register.
Raise the risk's probability to 100% and continue to manage it only in the risk register, where it is already recorded.
Close the risk as unsuccessfully treated, record the lesson in the lessons log and leave the solution to the supplier.
Immediately send the Project Board an exception report, because every risk that occurs requires a decision of the board.
explanation: A risk is an uncertain event; once it occurs it becomes an issue and is dealt with using the issue management technique (Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide, Implement), while the risk register records that the risk has occurred. Merely raising the probability to 100% confuses a risk with an issue and provides no procedure for assessment and decision. An exception report is necessary only if the assessment shows a forecast breach of the stage tolerances, which is not yet known.

scenario: The product description of the nurse call system for the internal medicine pavilion of a regional hospital states that the audible signalling in the corridor must reach a volume of at least 65 dB. During quality control, the system supplier's Team manager Martin Sykora found that the delivered speakers reach at most 60 dB and the supplier has no other type on offer. The Team manager reported this to project manager Jana Kralova.
question: How should the project manager classify this issue?
options: As an off-specification, because the product will not meet the quality specification stated in its product description.
As a request for change, because the product description will have to be changed to correspond to 60 dB.
As a concern, because it has not yet been decided whether the hospital will accept the lower volume or insists on 65 dB.
As a risk (threat), because it is not certain whether staff in the corridor will hear signalling at a volume of 60 dB.
explanation: An off-specification is a situation in which a product does not meet, or is forecast not to meet, its quality specifications – here 60 dB instead of the required 65 dB. A request for change would be a proposal to change the baseline, e.g. if users themselves wanted to change the specification; amending the specification may be one of the possible solutions, but the situation is captured as an off-specification. Failure to meet the specification is already a known fact, and it is therefore not a risk.

image.alt: The six types of issue in PRINCE2 7 and the five steps of the issue management technique: Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide, Implement.

scenario: In the internal medicine pavilion of a regional hospital it turned out that the floor covering in two storage rooms does not meet the slip-resistance class required in the product description. Head nurse Lucie Vavrova, in the Senior user role, said she does not mind it in the storerooms. According to the issue management approach no change authority was appointed and the Project Board decides on requests for change and off-specifications. Project manager Jana Kralova therefore recorded the deviation as a concession herself and closed the issue.
question: Was the project manager's decision appropriate, and why?
options: No, because acceptance of an off-specification without correction (a concession) may be approved only by the holder of delegated authority, here the Project Board.
No, because an off-specification is always removed and a concession cannot be granted for any product in PRINCE2 7.
Yes, because the Project manager may accept any deviation from the specification as long as it does not exceed the stage tolerances.
Yes, because the Senior user explicitly agreed to the deviation, and users' consent to a concession replaces the Project Board's decision.
explanation: A concession is an off-specification accepted without correction; it may be approved only by whoever the Project Board delegated authority to for this, and because no change authority was appointed, the Project Board itself decides. The project manager should have assessed the issue, prepared a recommendation (e.g. in an issue report) and submitted it for a decision. The Senior user's consent is an important input, but in itself it does not replace a decision according to the delegated authorities in the issue management approach.

image.alt: The six types of issue in PRINCE2 7 and the five steps of the issue management technique: Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide, Implement.

scenario: While configuring the new warehouse system, the supplier's Team manager found that the licence the logistics company has already purchased also includes a module for processing e-shop returns. The company had not counted on this module and so far processes returns manually in spreadsheets. According to the supplier, using it would require no further licence fees. Nobody has yet proposed switching the module on or changing the project scope; the Team manager merely passed the information on to project manager Eva Markova.
question: How should the project manager classify this fact at Capture?
options: As an issue of the business opportunity type, because it is an unexpected favourable finding that may benefit the user organisation.
As an opportunity in the risk register with the exploit response, because it is a positive uncertain event that should be exploited as fully as possible.
As a request for change, because using the returns module would extend the project scope beyond the approved baseline.
As an event external to the project, because the content of the licence was decided by the system supplier outside the project team.
explanation: In PRINCE2 7 a business opportunity is a type of issue: an unexpected favourable circumstance for the project or the user organisation that is already known and requires assessment. An opportunity in the risk register would be an uncertain future event, whereas here it is a established fact. If after assessment it is decided to use the module and extend the scope, a request for change will arise – but at the time of capture no change to the baseline had been proposed.

image.alt: The six types of issue in PRINCE2 7 and the five steps of the issue management technique: Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide, Implement.

scenario: During the second stage of the Citizen Portal project, parliament passed an amendment to the law under which all municipal portals must, within one year, support a new electronic signature format. The portal launch is planned in eight months and its approved scope does not provide for this format. Project manager Tomas Bures learned of the amendment from the media and is about to record it in the issue register.
question: What type of issue is this at the moment of capture?
options: Event external to the project – an event outside the project that affects it and whose consequences must be assessed.
Request for change – the amendment will require a change to the portal's approved baseline, so it is directly a request for change.
Off-specification – in its current form the portal will not support the new electronic signature format under the amendment.
Problem – the amendment has an immediate negative impact, because the portal already now fails to meet the requirements of the law in force.
explanation: The amendment is an event that occurred outside the project and affects its objectives, so it is captured as an issue of the event external to the project type and its impact on the business case, plans and risks is assessed. A request for change will probably emerge from the assessment, but only as a specific proposed change to the baseline. It is not an off-specification, because the products still correspond to their approved specification – an external requirement has changed.

image.alt: The six types of issue in PRINCE2 7 and the five steps of the issue management technique: Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide, Implement.

scenario: At the construction site of the internal medicine pavilion of a regional hospital, the only tower crane broke down this morning and the concrete pour of the third-floor ceiling had to be stopped. Site manager Petr Holub, in the Team manager role, estimates that the repair will take at least three days and reported it as an issue. No approved product or its specification is changed by this. Project manager Jana Kralova is recording the issue in the issue register.
question: What type of issue should the project manager record?
options: Problem, because it is an event that has already occurred and has an immediate negative impact on the progress of work.
Concern, because it will only become clear whether the three-day delay threatens the time tolerance of the work package.
Risk (threat), because the breakdown may lead to a delay and a reduce-type response needs to be planned.
Off-specification, because the ceiling will not be poured by the date stated in its product description.
explanation: A problem is an issue with an immediate negative impact – the halted concrete pour is a fact that has already occurred, and its impact on the stage plan will be clarified in the Assess step. A concern corresponds to a situation where the timing and impact are not yet apparent; here the impact is immediate and only its extent is yet to be evaluated. It is not an off-specification, because no product breaches its quality specifications and the product description contains no dates.

image.alt: The six types of issue in PRINCE2 7 and the five steps of the issue management technique: Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide, Implement.

scenario: The head of the logistics company's distribution centre asked that the new warehouse system, in addition to Czech labels, also print labels in German for Austrian customers. Project manager Eva Markova recorded the request in the issue register as a request for change and assessed its impact on the business case, risks and stage plan: the change would cost CZK 120,000 and extend the stage by a week. She now wants to continue following the issue management technique.
question: What should the project manager do as the next step?
options: Evaluate the options for resolution and recommend one to whoever decides on the change, because the Assess step is followed by the Recommend step.
Include the change directly in the supplier's work, because the assessment showed that both the cost and the stage extension fit within its tolerances.
Capture the request again as an off-specification against the product description of the printing module, which does not mention German labels.
Close the issue in the issue register and explain the impacts of the change in detail to the Project Board only in the end stage report at the end of the stage.
explanation: After Capture and assessing the impacts (Assess), the Recommend step follows: the project manager identifies and evaluates the options and recommends one of them to whoever is to decide on the change (Decide); only then is the change implemented (Implement). Including the change directly in the supplier's work would skip both the recommendation and the decision of the authorised person – the Project manager may decide on changes only if the Project Board has delegated this to them. A feature that the specification never required is not an off-specification.

image.alt: The six types of issue in PRINCE2 7 and the five steps of the issue management technique: Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide, Implement.

scenario: The Project Board of the Citizen Portal project delegated decisions on requests for change of low and medium severity to the head of the citizen services department (Senior user) as change authority, up to CZK 100,000 per change from a change budget of CZK 500,000. CZK 300,000 remains in the change budget. Project manager Tomas Bures has just assessed a request to modify the parking permit application form: medium severity, cost CZK 80,000, no impact on stage tolerances.
question: Who should decide on this request for change?
options: The Senior user as change authority, because the change is within the delegated severity, the per-change limit and the remaining change budget.
The Project manager, because the change has no impact on stage tolerances, and within tolerances the Project manager may decide on all changes.
The Executive, because they own the business case and decide as the sole accountable person on every change that costs anything.
The whole Project Board, because the steering board always decides on changes to the baseline and delegation to a change authority applies only to off-specifications.
explanation: The Project Board determines who may decide on changes; here it delegated authority to the Senior user as change authority within the severity and financial limits, which this change meets. The Project manager may decide on changes only if the Project Board has explicitly delegated this authority to them – merely staying within the stage tolerances is not enough. According to the issue management approach, delegation may apply to both requests for change and off-specifications.

scenario: The distribution centre manager, in the Senior user role, requires that the logistics company's new warehouse system also be connected to the new carrier's system, without which the company would not be able to dispatch shipments to a new key customer after launch. The assessment showed that the change would cost CZK 600,000 and its implementation would cause the cost and time tolerances of the second stage to be exceeded. The change authority has a limit of CZK 150,000 per change and the change budget is almost exhausted.
question: Which action should project manager Eva Markova take?
options: Prepare an exception report for the Project Board with the assessment, options and a recommendation, because the change would lead to a breach of the stage tolerances.
Split the change into several partial requests of up to CZK 150,000 and submit them sequentially to the change authority for approval within its limit.
Approve the change herself and cover the cost from the risk budget, because without the connection to the carrier the project would lose its justification in the business case.
Ask the supplier's Team manager to incorporate the change into the next sprints and to report its impacts continuously in checkpoint reports.
explanation: If implementing the change would lead to a forecast breach of the stage tolerances, it is no longer an ordinary decision within the delegated authorities but an exception, which the project manager escalates to the Project Board with an exception report containing options and a recommendation. Splitting the change into smaller parts would circumvent the limits that the Project Board set for the change authority. The project manager can neither approve the change nor fund it from the risk budget.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: The construction company's painter pointed out that the supplier currently does not have the chosen manufacturer's paint in stock for the storeroom in the internal medicine pavilion of a regional hospital, and proposed using paint from another manufacturer. The product description does not specify the manufacturer, only requirements for washability and resistance to disinfection, which the substitute paint demonstrably meets. The substitution has no impact on cost or deadlines. Project manager Jana Kralova agreed to the substitution and recorded it in the daily log, not in the issue register.
