question: Was this handling of the issue appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because an issue with no impact on the baseline that can be resolved informally may be recorded and dealt with by the Project manager in the daily log.
Yes, because the Project manager may approve all changes to the baseline up to the stage tolerances set for them by the Project Board.
No, because every issue must be recorded in the issue register and have an issue report, so that the Project Board can decide on it.
No, because a substitution of material is always an off-specification, which must be decided by the change authority or the Project Board.
explanation: At Capture it is decided whether to deal with the issue formally or informally; an issue that does not change any baselined product and can be resolved immediately needs only to be recorded in the daily log. Formal handling in the issue register and issue report is intended for issues that require assessment and a decision according to delegated authorities. The claim that the Project manager may approve all baseline changes up to the stage tolerances is wrong – changes are decided by the change authority, and by the Project manager only if this authority is delegated to them.

image.alt: The six types of issue in PRINCE2 7 and the five steps of the issue management technique: Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide, Implement.

scenario: The Citizen Portal of a statutory city is delivered iteratively by an external supplier in three-week sprints. The Senior user wants the head of the electronic services department, who works with the developers daily, to be able to adjust backlog item priorities on an ongoing basis without the Project Board having to approve every adjustment. Project manager Tomas Bures is preparing the issue management approach in the initiation stage.
question: Which tailoring of the issue management approach is appropriate in this project?
options: Propose that the Project Board appoint the head of the department as change authority for minor changes within clear limits and assess larger changes itself.
Exclude backlog changes from issue management entirely, because with iterative delivery requirements change continuously and change control would needlessly slow development.
Leave decisions on every change of priorities to the whole Project Board, because delegating authority for changes is not permissible with an external supplier.
Entrust the supplier's Team manager with deciding on all changes, because the supplier is best placed to assess the technical impact of changes on the whole system.
explanation: The Project Board may delegate decisions on changes to a change authority with clear limits (severity, scope, change budget), which are recorded in the issue management approach; with iterative delivery this makes it possible to change priorities flexibly without burdening the steering board. Removing changes from change control entirely contradicts PRINCE2 – even the continuous refinement of requirements takes place under baseline control. Entrusting all decisions to the supplier would take control of scope away from the users and the Executive.

scenario: The Project Board of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction project at a regional hospital approved a request for change: instead of two four-bed rooms, one isolation room with an anteroom will be built. The change is within the stage tolerances and construction work in this section has not yet started. Project manager Jana Kralova is now moving on to the Implement step.
question: What must the project manager ensure in the Implement step?
options: Update the product description and other affected baselined products, record the decision in the issue register and assign the work for implementation.
Give the change to the site manager verbally and leave the product description in the originally approved version, so that the project's valid baseline is preserved.
Prepare an exception report, because every change approved by the Project Board represents an exception and requires preparing a new exception plan.
Ask the Project Board for a new version of the PID and re-authorisation of the project, because an approved product change cancels the project's original authorisation.
explanation: In the Implement step the decided solution is carried out: affected baselined products are updated (a new version of the product description, stage plan, and possibly the work package description), the decision and status are recorded in the issue register and issue report, and the work is handed over for implementation. Leaving the product description in the original version would mean that the baseline does not match what is actually to be built. An approved change within tolerances requires neither an exception report nor re-authorisation of the project.

scenario: Site manager Petr Holub is the Team manager for the electrical installation work package in the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction project at a regional hospital. He found that, because of the late delivery of switchboards, the package will finish two weeks later than the time tolerance in the work package description allows. He therefore wrote an exception report and sent it directly to the hospital director as Executive and to the other members of the Project Board.
question: Was this action by the Team manager appropriate, and why?
options: No, because a forecast breach of the package tolerance must be escalated by the Team manager as an issue to the Project manager, who set the package tolerances.
No, because the Team manager should first use up the time contingency of the whole stage and send the exception report when the stage tolerance is breached.
Yes, because a breach of the work package tolerance is an exception that the steering board assesses as soon as possible and without intermediaries.
Yes, because the Team manager is an employee of the external supplier and turns directly to the Project Board with exception reports.
explanation: Work package tolerances are set by the Project manager in the work package description, and a Team manager therefore escalates to them, in the form of an issue, when a breach is forecast. The Project manager then assesses whether the situation can be resolved within the stage tolerances or whether an exception report needs to be submitted to the Project Board. The notion that a Team manager sends an exception report only when the stage tolerance is threatened is wrong – a Team manager never submits an exception report.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: The supplier's Team manager for the logistics company's new warehouse system reported an issue: the Integration with the transport system work package will finish six working days later than its time tolerance allows. Project manager Eva Markova found that if she postpones the follow-on warehouse worker training and moves two testers into testing from another work package of the stage that has time contingency, the stage will finish within both time and cost tolerance. She carried out these measures without turning to the Project Board and reported them in the next highlight report.
question: Did the project manager act appropriately, and why?
options: Yes, because within the stage tolerance the Project manager may act without the board; they then inform it of the measures taken in the highlight report.
Yes, because the Project manager sets the tolerances of both the stage and the work packages and can adjust them on their own according to the current situation in the project.
No, because a breach of a work package tolerance is always an exception, on which the whole Project Board decides on the basis of an exception report.
No, because any adjustment of the stage schedule is a change to the baseline that must be approved in advance by the change authority or the Project Board.
explanation: The manage by exception principle allows the Project manager to deal with deviations independently as long as the forecast remains within the stage tolerances set by the Project Board; they then report the measures taken in the regular highlight report. A breach of a work package tolerance is a reason for an issue to the Project manager, not an exception at steering board level. Stage tolerances are set not by the Project manager but by the Project Board, so the justification that they can adjust them on their own is wrong.

scenario: In the second stage of the Citizen Portal project it became apparent that integration with the town's records management service is much more laborious than assumed. Project manager Tomas Bures forecasts that the stage cost will exceed the tolerance set by the Project Board by about 15%, and no measure within his authority will change that. According to the forecast, the project should not exceed the project cost tolerance set by the steering board of the Digital City programme.
question: Which action should the Project manager take?
options: Submit an exception report with options and a recommendation to the Project Board, because it is an exception at stage level.
Prepare an exception plan for the rest of the stage and continue immediately according to it, so that no time is lost.
Turn directly to the programme steering board, because the breach concerns money that the programme allocated to the project.
Continue according to the stage plan and explain the deviation and its causes in detail to the Project Board in the end stage report.
explanation: A forecast breach of the stage tolerance is an exception: the Project manager escalates it immediately to the Project Board with an exception report describing the cause, consequences, options and recommendation. They prepare an exception plan only at the Project Board's request in the Managing a stage boundary process and it applies only after approval. Turning directly to the business layer would bypass the Project Board; moreover, according to the forecast the project tolerance is not breached.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: The project manager of the Citizen Portal project submitted an exception report to the Project Board: because of an amendment to the law, the second stage will finish five weeks later than the stage plan assumes, while the stage's time tolerance is +3 weeks. According to the forecast, however, the project as a whole will remain within the project time tolerance (+2 months), which was set by the steering board of the Digital City programme as the business layer. The Executive, the town hall secretary Michal Riha, proposes that the Project Board itself request an exception plan and approve it once complete. The Senior user objects that every exception must be decided by the programme steering board.
question: Is the Executive's intention appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because it is an exception within the stage tolerances, which the Project Board set, and the Project Board can therefore decide on the exception plan itself.
No, because every submitted exception report is decided by the business layer, which set the tolerances of the whole project.
Yes, because when approving an exception plan the Project Board may, as needed, itself also extend the tolerances of the whole project.
No, because an exception plan is prepared only when a breach of the project tolerances set by the business layer is threatened.
explanation: The Project Board sets the stage tolerances and therefore deals with stage-level exceptions itself: it can request an exception plan, which the Project manager prepares in Managing a stage boundary, and approve it in Authorize a stage or exception plan. The business layer decides only when a breach of the project tolerances that it set is forecast – which, according to the forecast, is not threatened here. The Project Board cannot extend the project tolerances itself, however.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: When authorising the stage, the Project Board of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction project at a regional hospital set that the project manager would send it a highlight report every week. In the second month of the stage only calm finishing work is under way, and project manager Jana Kralova therefore proposed to the board that highlight reports be sent once a month. The Project Board agreed to the proposal and Kralova has been sending reports monthly since. A project assurance officer objects that the frequency set when the stage was authorised can be changed only at the stage boundary.
question: Is the project manager's approach in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: Yes, because the frequency of highlight reports is determined by the Project Board, which can therefore change it during the stage as well at the project manager's proposal.
No, because the frequency of highlight reports set when the stage was authorised can be changed only at its boundary in Managing a stage boundary.
Yes, because the frequency of highlight reports is an internal matter for the project manager and the Project Board's agreement was merely a courtesy.
No, because highlight reports are an event-driven control and are sent only when the stage status changes significantly.
explanation: Highlight reports are a time-driven control and their frequency and form are set by the Project Board, to which the Project manager reports. The board can therefore adjust the frequency during the stage as well at the project manager's proposal – what matters is that it approved the change; the manager could not have introduced it alone. There is no need to postpone a change of frequency to the stage boundary, and highlight reports are not an event-driven control – examples of those are the end stage report or the exception report.

scenario: A logistics company has a financial year that ends on 31 March. The Project Board of the new warehouse system project requires project manager Eva Markova to send it a highlight report every 14 days and, in addition, to submit a summary report on the project's status as at 31 March for the annual closing. The supplier's Team manager will pass checkpoint reports to the project manager every Friday.
question: Which statement about the controls set up in this project is correct?
options: The report as at 31 March is an event-driven control, whereas the highlight and checkpoint reports are time-driven controls.
All three controls are time-driven, because they are tied to calendar dates known in advance or to regular intervals.
The report as at 31 March and the highlight reports are event-driven controls; only the checkpoint reports are time-driven.
The highlight reports are a time-driven control; the report as at 31 March and the checkpoint reports are event-driven controls.
explanation: Time-driven controls take place at regular intervals – typically highlight reports from the Project manager to the Project Board and checkpoint reports from the Team manager to the Project manager. Event-driven controls occur at a particular event, e.g. at the end of a stage, on completion of the PID, on an exception or at an organisational event such as the end of the financial year. The fact that the end of the financial year falls on a known date does not make it a regular control – it is an organisational event.

image.alt: Table of PRINCE2 7 reports: who prepares them for whom, when they arise and whether they are time-driven or event-driven.

scenario: The business case of the internal medicine pavilion reconstruction project at a regional hospital contains a sustainability objective: recycle at least 70% of construction waste. For the demolition stage the Project Board set a sustainability tolerance of 65–75% recycled waste. Midway through the stage, project manager Jana Kralova forecasts that recycling will reach only 55%, because the contracted recycling company has stopped accepting plasterboard. The stage's time and cost are within tolerance.
question: How should the project manager proceed?
options: Escalate the situation to the Project Board with an exception report, because a breach of the stage's sustainability tolerance is forecast.
Continue the stage and report the deviation only in the end project report, because sustainability is assessed for the project as a whole.
Record the deviation in the lessons log and do nothing further, because tolerances are not set for sustainability in PRINCE2.
Ask the site manager as Team manager to send the Project Board an exception report because of the sustainability deviation.
explanation: The seventh edition of PRINCE2 added sustainability as the seventh performance target, for which tolerances are set in the same way as for time or cost. A forecast that recycling will end up outside the stage tolerance is therefore an exception and the project manager escalates it with an exception report, even though the other targets are within tolerance. The claim that sustainability has no tolerance corresponds to the 6th edition, which worked with only six targets.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: At the end of the third sprint in the Citizen Portal project, Project manager Tomas Bures found that the supplier's effort estimates for integrations were, in all sprints, roughly 40% lower than the actual effort. The team has so far compensated by moving low-priority items to later sprints, so the stage remains within tolerances. Bures wants this finding to be taken into account when planning further stages and in the city's future projects.
question: Where should the Project manager record this finding?
options: In the lessons log, so that it can be used in further stages and included in the lessons report for the organisation.
In the daily log, because it is their own observation that does not require formal handling as an issue.
In the issue register as a problem, because the underestimated estimates have already caused items to be moved between sprints.
In the quality register, because the supplier's inaccurate estimates are a quality shortcoming of its work on products.
explanation: The lessons log serves to record lessons that can be used in this project (e.g. when planning further stages) and in future projects; the lessons report, through which lessons are passed to the organisation, is then prepared from it. The daily log is the Project manager's working diary for informal issues, actions and notes, and the lesson would get lost in it. Because the stage remains within tolerances and nothing needs to be decided, it is not a formal issue either.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records from the daily log to the product register.

scenario: The Citizen Portal project is part of the city's Digital City programme. The programme steering board set the project a cost tolerance of ±10% and a time tolerance of +2 months. The Project Board set a cost tolerance of ±5% and a time tolerance of +3 weeks for the second stage. The Payment gateway integration work package will be carried out by an external supplier and Project manager Tomas Bures is preparing its work package description.
question: Which statement about setting tolerances is correct in this project?
options: The package tolerances are set by the Project manager in the work package description, so that they fit within the tolerances of the second stage.
The package tolerances are set by the Project Board, because the package is carried out by an external supplier under a concluded commercial contract.
The Project manager may set the package tolerances up to the level of the project tolerances, i.e. ±10% of cost and +2 months.
The package tolerances are set by the supplier's Team manager in the team plan, which is then submitted to the Project Board for approval.
explanation: Tolerances are delegated top-down: the business layer (here the programme steering board) sets the project tolerances, the Project Board the stage tolerances and the Project manager the work package tolerances, which they record in the work package description. The Project manager cannot delegate more than they have themselves, so the package tolerances must fit within the stage tolerances, not the project tolerances. The fact that the package is carried out by an external supplier changes nothing – the package is authorised and its tolerances set by the Project manager.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: The logistics company's new warehouse system is delivered by an external supplier in two-week sprints. The work package description for the Inventory module sets a scope tolerance: all items with "must" priority must be delivered, items with "could" priority may be dropped. In the package's last sprint the supplier's Team manager found that they would not manage to deliver printing of inventory labels in the new design ("could" priority), and dropped it without consulting the project manager. They stated this in the regular checkpoint report.
question: Did the Team manager act appropriately, and why?
options: Yes, because dropping a "could" item is within the scope tolerance that the Project manager set for them in the work package description.
Yes, because with iterative delivery the Team manager may change the scope of sprints freely, as long as they keep to the package's deadline and cost.
No, because scope is not among the targets for which tolerances are set in PRINCE2 7, and every change is therefore a change to the baseline.
No, because the dropping of any function must always be decided by the Project Board, even if it is an item of the lowest priority.
explanation: Scope is one of the seven performance targets with a tolerance; with iterative delivery, the scope tolerance is often expressed by requirement priorities. The Team manager acted within the tolerance that the Project manager delegated to them in the work package description and reported the change in the checkpoint report. If it had been threatened that they would not deliver a "must" item, it would have been a forecast breach of tolerance and they would have had to pass an issue to the project manager.

scenario: Polabska University is preparing the construction of a new laboratory pavilion costing CZK 420 million. The rector, who commissions the project on behalf of the university (business layer), handed the investment department a short project mandate. At the same time he appointed Simona Kralova as project manager (Project manager) and asked her to choose the Executive herself from among the university's management once the project brief is ready. Simona has meanwhile started gathering inputs for the project brief.
question: Was this approach at the beginning of the Starting up a project process appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the Executive is appointed by the business layer as the first step of SU and the Project manager is appointed only by the Executive.
No, because both the Executive and the Project manager are appointed by the Project Board when it decides in the "Authorize initiation" activity.
Yes, because appointing all members of the project management team is the Project manager's task in the "Appoint the project management team" activity.
Yes, because it is enough to appoint the Executive before the project brief is submitted, so that they can assess the already completed scope of the project.
explanation: The first activity of SU is "Appoint the executive and the project manager": the business layer appoints the Executive, who then appoints the Project manager. The Executive is the single point of accountability for the project and owns the business case, so they must be in their role from the start and cannot be chosen retrospectively by the Project manager. The "Appoint the project management team" activity concerns filling the other roles, and the Project Board, which decides in "Authorize initiation", must already exist by then.

scenario: Krokus Bank is a regional bank that is replacing an obsolete mobile banking app with a new app, Krokus Mobil. Tomas Vesely has just been appointed Project manager and is starting the Starting up a project process. Three years ago the bank launched an app for corporate clients whose project significantly exceeded its budget because the security department was involved only shortly before launch. Tomas therefore studied the lessons report of that project, spoke to its then project manager and recorded his findings before he began preparing the outline business case and the initiation stage plan.
question: Was Tomas's conduct appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because in SU lessons from earlier projects should be assessed, so that they are reflected in the project brief and the initiation plan.
Yes, because in the "Capture previous lessons" activity lessons are recorded in the project mandate, which the Project manager supplements in SU.
No, because lessons are systematically evaluated only in the Closing a project process, when the lessons report for the organisation is produced.
No, because seeking lessons from other projects is the task of Project assurance, which must be independent of the Project manager.
explanation: Starting up a project contains the activity "Assess previous lessons" (in the 6th edition "Capture previous lessons") – the Learn from experience principle applies already before initiation, so that the mistakes of earlier projects are not repeated in the project brief or the initiation stage plan. Lessons are sought and recorded throughout the project; the lessons report at closure is only one of the moments when they are passed to the organisation. The project mandate is an input from the business layer and lessons are not added to it; moreover, everyone should seek lessons, not just Project assurance.

scenario: Polabska University is building a new laboratory pavilion. In the Starting up a project process, the Executive (bursar Karel Novak) and project manager Simona Kralova are putting together the project management team. A construction company will be selected in a public tender only during the first delivery stage. Simona therefore proposes that until then supplier interests on the Project Board be represented by the head of the university's technical department, whose designers are preparing the construction design documentation for the project, and that the team structure and role descriptions be updated once the construction company is selected.
question: Was Simona's proposal appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because in SU the roles needed for initiation are filled and the team structure can be updated at a stage boundary once the supplier is known.
Yes, because Senior supplier is an optional role and until the construction company is selected nobody representing the supplier need be on the Project Board.
No, because the Senior supplier role may be held only by a representative of an external supplier, not by a unit of the organisation commissioning the project.
No, because the composition of the Project Board must not be changed after the project brief is approved and the construction company should already be selected in SU.
explanation: The aim of SU is to have people appointed for initiation and key roles filled; supplier interests may initially be defended by an internal unit that provides specialist resources for the project – a supplier can be internal or external. The Project Board must have at least one Senior supplier, so the role cannot be left vacant. The project management team structure and role descriptions in the PID can be revised at a stage boundary (Managing a stage boundary) once the construction company is selected.

scenario: The Drogerie Lipa chain with 180 stores wants to introduce the Lipa Klub loyalty programme with a mobile app and integration with the point-of-sale systems. In the Starting up a project process the team is considering three solution options: in-house development, renting a ready-made SaaS platform, or extending the existing e-shop. Marketing prefers launching features in monthly increments, whereas the IT department prefers a one-off launch across the whole network. Project manager Alena Cermakova proposes postponing the choice of solution and delivery approach to initiation, where "all approaches will be prepared at once".
question: How should Alena proceed according to PRINCE2?
options: Evaluate the options already in SU and select the project approach (solution and delivery approach), because it belongs in the project brief.
Select the solution and delivery approach in IP within the "Agree the management approaches" activity and record them in the PID.
Leave the choice of solution to the Senior supplier, because the technical solution is decided by the supplier, not the Project Board.
Select the delivery approach only in the Managing a stage boundary process at the end of initiation, when the first delivery stage is planned.
explanation: One of the aims of SU is to evaluate alternative approaches and agree the project approach – the chosen solution and delivery approach (linear-sequential, iterative-incremental or hybrid). The "Select the project approach" activity serves this, and the result is part of the project brief, on the basis of which the board authorises initiation. "Agree the management approaches" in IP concerns the approaches to managing risks, issues, quality, communication and so on, not the choice of solution.

scenario: Polabska University has started the Starting up a project process for a new laboratory pavilion. The project mandate contains only a basic idea of the scope and an indicative cost estimate. The Executive, bursar Karel Novak, asked project manager Simona Kralova to have a detailed investment analysis with a net present value calculation, a detailed building budget by floor and a plan for measuring all benefits prepared before requesting authorisation of initiation. Preparation would take two months and external consultants would cost CZK 1.2 million.
question: Was the Executive's request appropriate, and why?
options: No, because SU is only meant to verify whether the project is worth initiating; an outline business case is enough for that and details come only in IP.
No, because the Senior user, who is responsible for specifying benefits, prepares the business case in SU and the Executive merely approves it.
Yes, because in the "Authorize initiation" activity the Project Board approves the full business case together with the project plan.
Yes, because the Ensure continued business justification principle requires a full business case before initiation begins.
explanation: The purpose of SU is to answer, with proportionate effort, whether this is a viable and worthwhile project, and to prepare inputs for the decision on initiation; at this stage the justification takes the form of an outline business case in the project brief. Detailed analyses and the full business case belong in IP (the "Prepare the full business case" activity), whose cost the board knowingly authorises. The Ensure continued business justification principle applies in SU as well, but it does not require a full business case.

scenario: In the Starting up a project process for the Lipa Klub loyalty programme (Drogerie Lipa chain), project manager Alena Cermakova is preparing the project brief. The Senior user, marketing director Katerina Urbanova, refuses for now to specify how quickly the till must read a loyalty card or how many stores must be involved at launch, because "that will become clear only during testing". She proposes that the project product description be written only at the start of the last delivery stage.
question: How should Alena react according to PRINCE2?
options: Insist that the project product description with users' expectations and acceptance criteria be created already in SU as part of the project brief.
Agree, because acceptance criteria are defined in the Closing a project process within the "Confirm project acceptance" activity.
Agree and record the missing criteria as a risk for now, because according to PRINCE2 the project product description is created only in IP together with the project plan.
Ask the Senior supplier to set the acceptance criteria themselves, because they are responsible for the quality of the products delivered by the project.
explanation: The project product description is part of the project brief and is created already in SU; it contains users' quality expectations, acceptance criteria and the method of acceptance. One aim of SU is, among other things, not to build initiation on unverified assumptions about scope, deadlines, acceptance criteria and constraints. The criteria can be refined later through controlled change, but they cannot be postponed until the end – and they are formulated by the users, not the supplier.

scenario: The project for the new Krokus Mobil app at the regional Krokus Bank is in the Starting up a project process. Project manager Tomas Vesely has finished the project brief including the outline business case and the project product description. Executive Jana Horakova wants to submit the brief to the Project Board as soon as possible and proposes that Tomas draw up the initiation stage plan (how much time, how many people and how much money will be needed to prepare the PID) only as the first step of the Initiating a project process. Tomas insists that he will prepare the initiation stage plan still in SU and submit it to the board together with the project brief.
question: Is Tomas's position in line with PRINCE2, and why?
options: Yes, because the initiation stage plan is created in SU and the Project Board approves it together with the project brief in the "Authorize initiation" activity.
No, because the initiation stage is not planned separately; its work is included in the project plan, which the board approves in "Authorize the project".
Yes, because in the "Authorize initiation" activity the board also approves the project plan, whose first part is the initiation stage plan.
No, because the first activity of IP is to plan the initiation stage and only then are the tailoring requirements agreed.
explanation: The initiation stage plan is prepared by the Project manager in SU (the "Plan the initiation stage" activity) and the Project Board approves it in DP together with the project brief in "Authorize initiation" – the board thus knowingly decides on the time and cost that initiation will consume. The initiation stage is the first management stage and is planned with a separate stage plan; the project plan is created only in IP and the board approves it in "Authorize the project". The first activity of IP is "Agree tailoring requirements", not planning initiation.

scenario: The Project Board of the Krokus Mobil project at the regional Krokus Bank is assessing the project brief and the initiation stage plan in the "Authorize initiation" activity. The outline business case gives as the only reason for the project "a more modern look of the app", contains no cost estimate or comparison of options and does not mention the bank's strategic goal of increasing the share of clients actively using the mobile channel. Executive Jana Horakova nevertheless proposes approving initiation, because "the details will be worked out in the PID".
question: How should the Project Board proceed according to PRINCE2?
options: Not authorise initiation yet and require the outline business case to be supplemented, so that it is clear the project is worth investing in initiation.
Authorise initiation, because the full business case is created only in IP and the project's justification is not yet assessed when initiation is authorised.
Authorise initiation and instruct Project assurance to finish the business case during the initiation stage instead of the Project manager.
Return the project brief to the business layer, because the business layer, not the Project Board, decides on starting initiation and on its budget.
explanation: The aim of SU is to demonstrate that starting initiation is justified, and the Project Board verifies this in "Authorize initiation" – the business case is checked at every board decision, the first time precisely as an outline business case. A brief without a cost estimate, without options and without a link to the organisation's objectives does not allow such a decision. The fact that the full business case is created only in IP does not mean that the justification for initiation is not assessed.

scenario: Krokus Bank is carrying out a digitalisation programme and one of its projects is the new mobile banking app Krokus Mobil. Programme management handed the project a detailed mandate: it contains an agreed scope, justification within the programme's business case, a chosen solution and an appointed Executive and Project manager. Project manager Tomas Vesely therefore put together, within two days, a brief project brief based on the mandate, which refers to the programme's business case for the justification, added the initiation stage plan and asked the Project Board to authorise initiation.
question: Was this shortened course of the Starting up a project process appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because SU can be tailored and significantly shortened, provided its objectives are met and the board explicitly decides on starting initiation.
Yes, because for projects within a programme the project brief is a mere formality that the board approves without assessing the project's justification.
No, because SU must always be carried out in full, so that a separate outline business case, entirely independent of the programme's business case, is produced.
No, because the decision to start initiation of a project within a programme is made by programme management, not by the project's Project Board.
explanation: If the programme supplies information at the level of a project brief, SU can be very short – this too is a tailoring of the method. What matters is that the objectives of SU (verified justification, appointed roles, project brief and initiation plan) are met and that the Project Board explicitly decides on starting initiation in DP in the "Authorize initiation" activity. The justification of a project within a programme may be based on the programme's business case, so a separate independent outline business case is not necessary.

scenario: The Krokus Mobil project at the regional Krokus Bank has been authorised for initiation. The bank has an internal project methodology with mandatory document templates. Given the supplier's agile way of working, Project manager Tomas Vesely wants to keep both the issue register and the risk register in the same online tool as the product backlog and, instead of written highlight reports, to provide the Project Board with a shared dashboard with commentary every two weeks. He wants to agree these adjustments with the board and the teams.
question: When and where should these adjustments be agreed and documented according to PRINCE2?
options: In IP in the "Agree tailoring requirements" activity; they are recorded in the PID, which the board approves in "Authorize the project".
In SU in the "Select the project approach" activity; they are recorded in the project brief, which is no longer updated after initiation.
In CS at the first "Report highlights", when it becomes clear whether the dashboard suits the board; they are recorded in the daily log.
In SB at the end of initiation in the "Prepare next stage plan" activity, because tailoring concerns only the delivery stages.
explanation: One of the aims of IP is to determine how the organisation's policies, methods and standards will be applied in the specific project; the "Agree tailoring requirements" activity serves this. Agreed tailoring – for example registers in a single tool or a dashboard instead of a written report – is recorded in the PID, so the Project Board approves it when authorising the project. The project approach in SU deals with the choice of solution and delivery approach, not with tailoring the management products and reporting.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records from the daily log to the product register.

scenario: The Lipa Klub loyalty programme of the Drogerie Lipa chain is in the Initiating a project process. The Executive, sales director Michal Svoboda, requires it to be clearly defined who may approve requests for changes to app functions and from which budget they will be paid. The Senior user for store operations also points out that sales assistants will have to change established procedures at the tills and will need to be prepared for it. Project manager Alena Cermakova is preparing inputs for the PID.
question: Where should Alena incorporate the rules for approving changes to functions and the change budget?
options: Into the issue management approach, because it determines the change authority and change budget; it is agreed in IP and becomes part of the PID.
Into the change management approach, because in the PID it describes how the project manages changes to the baseline and who decides on them.
Into the communication management approach, because requests for changes to functions come from stakeholders and the board is informed about them.
Into the project brief, which is supplemented in IP with change control rules, so a separate issue management approach is not needed.
explanation: The rules for managing changes to the baseline – the severity scale, the determination of the change authority and the change budget – belong in the issue management approach, which is agreed together with the other approaches in IP in the "Agree the management approaches" activity. The change management approach deals with organisational change among the people the project will affect; it covers preparing the sales assistants, not approving changes to functions. The project brief is not extended in IP; it is replaced by the PID.

image.alt: Two containers: the PID with nine management approaches and the project log with six records from the daily log to the product register.

scenario: Polabska University is in the initiation stage of the new laboratory pavilion project. Project manager Simona Kralova is preparing the project plan according to the university template: the plan contains a list of activities of the individual departments (investment, legal and technical) with deadlines and budget, but does not state what products are to be created in the individual stages. The project product description from SU, which describes the finished pavilion and the acceptance criteria, is not used in the plan in any way.
question: Was this way of preparing the project plan appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the plan should be based on the project product description and on the breakdown of products including their descriptions and dependencies.
No, because the project plan is not prepared in IP; it is created only in SB at the end of initiation together with the stage plan of the first delivery stage.
Yes, because the project plan is a high-level plan for the Project Board and products are defined only in stage plans and work packages.
Yes, because PRINCE2 does not prescribe a planning technique and tailoring allows planning by the activities of the organisation's departments.
explanation: The project plan is created in IP (the "Prepare the project plan" activity) using the PRINCE2 planning technique, which starts with defining and analysing products – for a project plan it is based on the project product description, the product breakdown structure, product descriptions and the product flow diagram. A plan made up only of departmental activities contradicts the Focus on products principle and gives the board no yardstick for what is to be delivered in which stage. Tailoring may change the form of the plan, not the focus on products.

scenario: The new laboratory pavilion project of Polabska University is in the initiation stage. Project manager Simona Kralova wanted to save time, and so right at the start of initiation she finished the full business case based on the estimates from the outline business case. The project plan being drawn up, however, shows that because of an archaeological survey the construction will take eight months longer and cost CZK 35 million more. Simona wants to submit the PID with the business case unchanged, so as not to delay authorisation of the project.
question: Was Simona's solution appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the full business case should be based on the costs, timescales and risks from the project plan, and must therefore be updated.
No, because the full business case is prepared only in the Managing a stage boundary process at the end of the initiation stage.
Yes, because the business case is owned by the Executive and the Project manager may no longer interfere with it during initiation.
Yes, because changes to costs and deadlines are reflected in the business case only in the "Update the business case" activity at a stage boundary.
explanation: In IP the full business case is prepared (the "Prepare the full business case" activity) on the basis of the project plan – its costs and timescale – and the assessed risks. The board in "Authorize the project" must decide on current data; a business case that does not take into account a construction that is eight months longer and CZK 35 million more expensive is not sufficient for an investment decision. The "Update the business case" activity in SB serves for updating at subsequent stage boundaries, not for correcting an incomplete basis for authorisation.

scenario: In the Initiating a project process, Project manager Tomas Vesely has finished the PID of the Krokus Mobil project at the regional Krokus Bank, including the full business case, project plan and all management approaches. Besides the initiation stage, the project has three more delivery stages. Executive Jana Horakova wants the Project Board at its next meeting not only to authorise the project but also to allow work to start in the first delivery stage.
question: What else must Tomas prepare for this to be possible according to PRINCE2?
options: The stage plan of the first delivery stage, because without it the board will not authorise the stage; it is prepared in Managing a stage boundary.
Team plans of all of the supplier's teams for the whole project, which the Project Board approves together with the PID in "Authorize the project".
Work package descriptions for all three delivery stages, because the Project Board authorises them in "Authorize the project".
An updated project brief, which together with the PID forms the basis for the board's decision in the "Authorize the project" activity.
explanation: When the PID is complete, the boundary of the initiation stage arrives: in the Managing a stage boundary process the Project manager prepares the stage plan of the next stage (the "Prepare next stage plan" activity) and requests its start. In DP the board then authorises the project on the basis of the PID and the first delivery stage at the same time. Team plans are optional and are created in MP, work packages are authorised by the Project manager in Controlling a stage, and the project brief is not updated after initiation – it was replaced by the PID.

image.alt: Grid of the seven PRINCE2 7 processes by project phase (pre-project, initiation stage, subsequent stages, final stage) and by the levels of directing, managing and delivering.

scenario: The Project Board of the new laboratory pavilion of Polabska University is assessing the PID in the "Authorize the project" activity. The rector (business layer) set a cost tolerance of ±5% for the project in the mandate. The project plan, however, because of the uncertain condition of the subsoil, shows a higher risk of cost overrun. Executive Karel Novak therefore asked the rector to widen the project cost tolerance, and the board meanwhile set the tolerances of the first delivery stage within the existing ±5%.
question: Was the approach of the Executive and the board appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because project tolerances are set and changed only by the business layer, whereas stage tolerances are set by the board within them.
Yes, because the board may change both project and stage tolerances itself, and the request addressed to the rector was merely a courtesy.
No, because the board should itself have raised the project tolerance when approving the PID, since the project plan shows a higher risk of overrun.
No, because stage tolerances are set by the Project manager in the stage plan and the board merely takes note of them when authorising the project.
explanation: Project tolerances are set by the business layer (here the rector) and only it can change them; within them the Project Board sets stage tolerances and the Project manager sets work package tolerances. If the project plan shows that ±5% is unrealistic, the right thing is to discuss the situation with the business layer, not to change the tolerance in the PID on one's own initiative. The stage plan is prepared by the Project manager, but the stage tolerances are set by the board.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: The project for the new Krokus Mobil app at the regional Krokus Bank is in the second stage, which is focused on development. In the "Authorize a work package" activity, Project manager Tomas Vesely is preparing a work package for developing the payments module for Ondrej Kriz, Team manager of the external supplier AppNest. The stage plan has a cost tolerance of ±10% and a time tolerance of ±3 weeks. The supplier's team works in two-week sprints.
question: Which entry is the most appropriate to include in the work package description?
options: A checkpoint report after every sprint; tolerances of ±5% cost and ±1 week; if a breach is threatened, the Team manager must raise an issue.
A highlight report after every sprint sent directly to the Project Board; package tolerances identical to the stage tolerances, i.e. ±10% and ±3 weeks.
A checkpoint report after every sprint; tolerances of ±15% cost and ±4 weeks so that the supplier has a margin; if a breach is forecast, they raise an issue.
The package tolerances are set by the Project Board in "Authorize a stage or exception plan"; the Team manager reports the package status only in the end stage report.
explanation: The work package description is the formal handover of work to the Team manager: it contains, among other things, the package tolerances, the frequency of checkpoint reports and the way of escalation. Package tolerances are set by the Project manager and must fit within the stage tolerances – with ±15% and ±4 weeks the package could breach the limits that the board set for the Project manager without the Project manager learning of it in time. Highlight reports are sent to the board by the Project manager, not the Team manager, and the Team manager raises an issue to the Project manager when a breach of the package tolerances is threatened.

scenario: The new laboratory pavilion of Polabska University is at the rough construction phase. Project manager Simona Kralova handed over to the site manager of the supplier StavPol, Pavel Holub (Team manager), a work package description for roofing the building with a deadline at the end of November. Before agreeing to the package, Pavel drew up a team plan, from which it followed that, because of the delivery time of the roof panels, the deadline is realistic only with a tolerance of two weeks. He therefore negotiated an adjustment of the time tolerance with Simona and only then accepted the package.
question: Was Pavel's conduct appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because on accepting a package the Team manager should verify its feasibility, if necessary with a team plan, and agree the conditions with the Project manager.
Yes, because the team plan drawn up by the Team manager replaces the work package description and sets new binding tolerances for the package.
No, because the work package description is an instruction from the Project manager that the Team manager must accept unchanged and deal with difficulties only in checkpoint reports.
No, because the team plan must be approved by the Project Board in the "Give ongoing direction" activity before the work package is accepted.
explanation: In MP, in the "Accept a work package" activity, the Team manager agrees the work package description with the Project manager – the products, deadlines, tolerances and reporting method – and may draw up a team plan to verify that the work can be done within the given limits. The aim of MP is for the assigned work to be authorised and agreed, not unilaterally ordered. A team plan is optional, is agreed with the Project manager and does not replace the work package description.

scenario: The Lipa Klub loyalty programme of the Drogerie Lipa chain is in the integration stage. Team manager Jakub Reznicek leads a team connecting the app to the stores' point-of-sale systems. Tests showed that an older type of till in 40 stores requires a firmware modification, and the package will therefore be delayed by three weeks, while the time tolerance in the work package description is only one week. Jakub did not wait for the Friday checkpoint report and raised an issue with project manager Alena Cermakova the same day. The Senior user for store operations reproached him that, because of the impact on the stores, he should have written directly to her and the Executive so that they could decide how to proceed.
question: Was Jakub's conduct appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because a forecast breach of the package tolerance should be reported by the Team manager to the Project manager immediately by raising an issue.
No, because the Team manager should first have prepared an exception plan for their package and submitted it to the Project Board for approval.
No, because according to the Manage by exception principle a forecast breach of tolerance is escalated directly to the Project Board.
Yes, because every issue from a Team manager is an exception, which the Project manager must pass to the board without further assessment.
explanation: Work package tolerances are set by the Project manager, so their forecast breach is escalated to them: in MP the Team manager raises an issue as soon as they forecast the breach, and does not wait for the regular checkpoint report. The Project manager then in CS assesses whether they can handle the situation within the stage tolerances or must escalate to the board – it is not automatically an exception for the board. Exception plans are not prepared for work packages, and management by exception means escalating one level up, not bypassing the Project manager.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: The construction of the new laboratory pavilion of Polabska University is in the third stage. A checkpoint report shows that the delivery of the ventilation system will be delayed by ten days, which exceeds the tolerance of the relevant work package. Project manager Simona Kralova verified that if she moves the electrical installation ahead of the ventilation, the stage will fit within its time and cost tolerances. She agreed the change with both Team managers, amended the work package descriptions and the stage plan and informed the Project Board in the next highlight report.
question: Was Simona's conduct appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because the Project manager may adopt measures keeping the stage within its tolerances without the board in the "Take corrective action" activity.
Yes, because a breach of a work package tolerance is an exception, which the Project manager resolves with their own exception plan.
No, because every change to the stage plan must be approved by the Project Board in the "Authorize a stage or exception plan" activity before it is made.
No, because the reallocation of work between teams of different suppliers is decided by the Senior supplier, who is responsible for supplier resources.
explanation: In CS, in the "Take corrective action" activity, the Project manager may resolve deviations on their own as long as the stage remains within the tolerances set by the board – this is the essence of management by exception. Adjusting work packages and updating the stage plan within tolerances falls within their authority and the board learns of the status from the highlight report. Exception plans are not prepared for work packages, and board approval would be necessary only when a breach of the stage tolerance is forecast.

scenario: The Krokus Mobil project at the regional Krokus Bank is in the second stage. Project manager Tomas Vesely found that a new regulatory requirement for strong payment authentication will require further development costing CZK 2.4 million, whereas the stage cost tolerance is ±CZK 1.5 million and the change budget is already exhausted. Two months remain until the end of the stage and Tomas hopes to save part of the cost in testing.
question: What should Tomas do?
options: Immediately submit an exception report with options and a recommendation to the board, because a breach of the stage tolerance is threatened.
Prepare an exception plan for the rest of the stage in the Managing a stage boundary process and submit it to the board for approval.
Take corrective action in testing and inform the Project Board of the outcome in the end stage report at the end of the stage.
Ask the change authority to increase the change budget, so that the new development fits within the stage tolerances without involving the board.
explanation: A forecast that the stage will exceed the cost tolerance is an exception: in CS, in the "Escalate issues and risks" activity, the Project manager escalates it immediately with an exception report, not only at the end of the stage or after an actual breach. The board decides on the basis of it, and only at its request does the Project manager prepare an exception plan in SB. The change budget is set by the board; the change authority cannot increase it itself.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set top-down and exceptions are escalated bottom-up.

scenario: When authorising the project, the Project Board of the Lipa Klub loyalty programme of the Drogerie Lipa chain set that it would receive a highlight report every two weeks. In the third stage everything is going according to plan, so project manager Alena Cermakova stopped sending highlight reports, saying she will get in touch "when something happens". The Executive learns about the status of the stage only from informal conversations in the corridor.
question: Was Alena's decision appropriate, and why?
options: No, because the highlight report is a time-driven control and the board should receive it at the agreed interval even when there are no problems.
No, because according to PRINCE2 the Project manager sends a highlight report every week regardless of agreement with the board.
Yes, because according to the Manage by exception principle the Project Board is informed only when a breach of one of the stage tolerances is threatened.
Yes, because the Project Board is informed about the progress of the stage by checkpoint reports, which Team managers send directly to the Executive.
explanation: Highlight reports are a time-driven control: in the "Report highlights" activity the Project manager sends them to the board at the frequency that the board set. Management by exception does not mean that the board receives no regular information – it means that it need not intervene until a breach of tolerances is threatened. Checkpoint reports are intended for the Project manager, not the board.

image.alt: Table of PRINCE2 7 reports: who prepares them for whom, when they arise and whether they are time-driven or event-driven.

scenario: In the second stage of the Krokus Mobil project, Senior user Petr Dvorak, director of the Krokus Bank branch network, visited the supplier's development team and asked the developers to add booking of appointments at a branch to the app. This function is not in the scope of the stage or in the product descriptions. The developers started working on it and the Team manager mentioned it to Project manager Tomas Vesely only in a checkpoint report.
question: How should Tomas proceed according to PRINCE2?
options: Capture the request as a request for change, because it is outside scope, and after assessing the impact submit it to the change authority or the board.
Include the function in the work, because the Senior user is a Project Board member and their instruction is a board decision in "Give ongoing direction".
Include the function in the work, pay for it from the risk budget and manage it as an unforeseen event that has already occurred.
Ask the Team manager for an exception report, because work outside scope means a breach of the work package tolerance.
explanation: Board members direct the project in DP through the Project manager, not by direct instructions to the team, and the board is not a democratic body – the Executive decides. A new function outside the approved scope is a request for change: the Project manager captures it in CS ("Capture issues and risks"), assesses the impact, and it is decided by the change authority, or by the Project Board if the change exceeds the delegated authority; in the meantime the team should work according to the authorised package. The risk budget serves for risk responses, not for scope changes.

image.alt: The six types of issue in PRINCE2 7 and the five steps of the issue management technique: Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide, Implement.

scenario: In the third stage of the Lipa Klub loyalty programme, two Senior users disagree on priorities: the marketing director wants to finish personalised offers in the app first, while the head of store operations insists on earlier connection of self-service tills. Both options fit within the stage tolerances, but they have a different impact on the expected benefits. Project manager Alena Cermakova is not sure which priority to choose.
question: How should Alena proceed according to PRINCE2?
options: Ask the Project Board for advice (request for advice), because a dispute over priorities with an impact on benefits goes beyond her role.
Issue an exception report, because disagreement among board members threatens the benefits and requires an exception plan.
Let the Team managers decide the order, because planning work within a stage is a matter for the teams, not the board.
Postpone the decision to the end of the stage and present both options in the end stage report in the Managing a stage boundary process.
explanation: When the Project manager needs a decision or guidance that goes beyond their role – here a dispute between two Senior users over a priority with an impact on benefits – they ask the board for advice. The board responds in DP with the "Give ongoing direction" activity (in the 6th edition "Give ad hoc direction") and the Executive has the final say, because the board is not a democratic body. An exception report is appropriate only when a breach of tolerances is forecast, and postponing the decision to the end of the stage would needlessly delay the work.

scenario: During the second stage of the Lipa Klub loyalty programme, the board of the Drogerie Lipa chain (business layer) informed Executive Michal Svoboda that the company has signed a partnership with a large bank and within a year will introduce a joint payment card with a loyalty function. This may fundamentally affect the programme's expected benefits. Project manager Alena Cermakova does not yet know about this and the stage is running within tolerances.
question:
Which two actions should the Project Board take in this situation?
1. Within the "Give ongoing direction" activity, inform the project manager of the board's decision.
2. Ask the project manager to assess the impact on the business case and, depending on the result, decide on how to proceed.
3. Wait until the end of the stage, because the stage is running within tolerances, and assess the impact only in "Authorize a stage or exception plan".
4. Request extraordinary checkpoint reports from the Team managers and decide on adjustments to work packages directly with them.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 3
3 and 4
1 and 4
explanation: "Give ongoing direction" also includes responding to external influences, for example a business layer decision that changes the context of the project. The board should pass the information to the project manager and ask them to assess the impact on the business case (an issue of the event external to the project type); depending on the result it then decides whether to continue, request an exception plan or close the project prematurely. Waiting until the end of the stage would weaken the Ensure continued business justification principle, and work packages are managed by the Project manager, not the board.

scenario: In the activity “Evaluate stage status”, Krokus Mobil project manager Tomas Vesely regularly reviews not only checkpoint reports and the stage plan but also the risk register, the issue register and the business case. At the latest evaluation he found that a competing bank had launched a similar application and that Krokus Bank's marketing now expects a third fewer new users than the business case assumes. Tomas recorded the event as an issue, had its impact on benefits assessed and, because the benefits forecast falls outside tolerance, submitted an exception report to the Project Board.
question: Was Tomas's action appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because in CS not only time and cost but also risks, issues and the continued business justification are monitored, and a threatened exception is escalated.
Yes, because under PRINCE2 every event external to the project is escalated to the board by an exception report, regardless of tolerances.
No, because the business case is not assessed during a stage; its update belongs exclusively to the Managing a stage boundary process.
No, because the impact on benefits should have been assessed by the Senior user, who should have escalated it directly to the business layer himself, without the Project manager.
explanation: The objectives of CS include keeping risks and issues under control and continually monitoring the business case; when evaluating stage status, the Project manager therefore also assesses risks, issues and the continued business justification. The launch of a competing application is an issue (an event external to the project); an exception report is appropriate because the assessment showed a forecast outside tolerance, not because the event is external. The business case is updated regularly in SB, but it must be monitored throughout the stage.

scenario: Ondrej Kriz, Team manager of the supplier AppNest, notified Krokus Bank's Project manager Tomas Vesely that the work package “Payments Module” for the Krokus Mobil application was complete. According to the product description, the module must pass a penetration test by the bank's security department before approval. The quality register, however, contains no record of this test, and Ondrej claims that the test “will take place later as part of overall testing”.
question: How should Tomas proceed in the activity “Receive completed work package”?
options: Treat the package as complete only after the quality check according to the product description and approval of the product by the approver.
Accept the package, because the Team manager decides on the quality of the delivered products and the Project manager merely records his completion notification.
Accept the package and merely record the missing penetration test in the lessons log as a lesson for further work packages in the following stages.
Return the package to the Team manager and ask him to prepare an exception plan for the missing test for approval by the Project Board.
explanation: When receiving a completed package, the Project manager verifies that the products have passed the quality check required in the product description and have been approved; records of this are provided by the quality register and the product register. The objective of CS is that the agreed products meet quality expectations and are accepted – without the penetration test, this condition is not met. Exception plans are not prepared for work packages, and the lessons log cannot replace the missing quality check.

scenario: The development team of the supplier AppNest works on the Krokus Mobil application using Scrum. In the work package description, which Team manager Ondrej Kriz agreed with Krokus Bank's Project manager Tomas Vesely, it is agreed that instead of written checkpoint reports Tomas will receive the package status at the sprint review every two weeks and continuously from a shared Kanban board, including a forecast of tolerance achievement. The tailoring described in the PID allows such an approach.
question: Was this way of reporting appropriate in the Managing product delivery process, and why?
options: Yes, because checkpoints can be adapted to the team's way of working, provided the Project manager receives a reliable status and forecast at the agreed frequency.
Yes, because with an iterative-incremental way of delivery the Managing product delivery process does not apply and is replaced by Scrum.
No, because the checkpoint report is a mandatory written management product whose form and content must not be changed by tailoring under any circumstances.
No, because the form and frequency of checkpoints are decided by the Project Board and cannot be agreed in the work package description.
explanation: The objective of MP is that the Project manager receives accurate information about progress at the agreed frequency; the frequency and form of checkpoints are agreed in the work package description. PRINCE2 7 expects tailoring – management products can be adapted or combined, for example written checkpoints can be replaced by oral ones or by agile ceremonies, as long as their purpose is preserved. MP applies to any way of delivery; Scrum does not replace it, it only influences its form.

scenario: The Drogerie Lipa chain is introducing the Lipa Klub loyalty programme with an application connected to the stores' checkout systems. The team of Team manager Jakub Reznicek completed the work package connecting the checkouts in ten pilot stores; the products passed quality checks and were approved. Because the team had spare capacity, Jakub immediately started connecting another 50 stores, which the stage plan assumes only a month later, and informed project manager Alena Cermakova about it only in the next checkpoint report.
question: Was Jakub's action appropriate, and why?
options: No, because he should have notified completion of the package and waited with further work until the Project manager authorised it with a new work package.
No, because connecting further stores is approved in advance by the Project Board as part of the activity “Give ongoing direction”.
Yes, because a Team manager may, within the stage tolerances, start work on his own that is included in the approved stage plan.
Yes, because the Team manager decides the order of work, and a checkpoint report is sufficient for informing the Project manager.
explanation: The team's work starts only when the Project manager authorises a work package in CS (“Authorize a work package”) and it is accepted in MP; after completing the package, the Team manager notifies its completion (“Notify work package completion”). The objective of MP is that the work assigned to the team is authorised and agreed – even if it is work from the stage plan, nobody has yet agreed products, tolerances or deadlines for it. The board does not authorise work packages; that is the Project manager's authority.

scenario: Load tests of the Krokus Mobil application showed that the system can handle 8,000 concurrently logged-in users, whereas the product description requires 10,000. This is an off-specification. According to the issue management approach in the PID, changes and deviations up to CZK 300,000 are decided by the change authority, made up of a representative of the Senior user and the bank's chief architect; above this limit the Project Board decides. The fix would cost CZK 900,000 and fits within the stage tolerances.
question: Who should, according to PRINCE2, decide how to deal with this off-specification?
options: The Project Board, because the cost exceeds the change authority's limit; the Project manager submits an issue report with options and a recommendation to it.
The change authority, because it decides on every off-specification regardless of cost, as long as the change fits within the stage tolerances.
The Project manager, because the fix fits within the stage tolerances, so he can approve it himself in the activity “Take corrective action”.
The Senior supplier, because the off-specification arose in the supplier's product and the supplier is responsible for its technical quality.
explanation: A request for change and an off-specification are decided by whomever the board has delegated this authority to – here the change authority up to CZK 300,000; above this limit the Project Board retained the decision. The Project manager captures and assesses the issue in CS and, because it exceeds the delegated authority, escalates it to the board (activity “Escalate issues and risks”) with options and a recommendation. The fact that the fix fits within the stage tolerances does not make it a corrective action within the Project manager's authority.

scenario: The second stage of the Lipa Klub loyalty programme is being delivered iteratively-incrementally. Project manager Alena Cermakova authorises a work package for the internal development team as a three-month timebox with a fixed deadline and budget. The scope is given in the work package description as a prioritised list of features: the mandatory features must be delivered, while for the less important ones it is agreed that the team may drop them if time runs short. The product descriptions of the mandatory features contain quality specifications.
question: Was such a set-up of the work package appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because in iterative delivery time and cost can be fixed and tolerance applied to the scope of the less important features.
Yes, because in iterative delivery work package tolerances are not set and the team determines the scope itself according to capacity.
No, because a work package must have a fixed scope of all products and tolerances can be set only for time and cost.
No, because only the Project Board may decide on dropping any feature, so scope tolerance cannot be delegated to the team.
explanation: Tolerances can be set for all seven performance targets, including scope. In iterative-incremental delivery, time and cost of a timebox are typically fixed and flexibility is left in the scope – prioritised requirements, of which the less important ones can be dropped within tolerance. The Project manager sets this tolerance in the work package description; the quality of the mandatory features is not reduced, because it is protected by the quality specifications in the product descriptions.

scenario: The project of the new laboratory pavilion of Polabska University has four stages, including the initiation stage, and the last of them is now under way – completion of the construction, fitting out of the laboratories and final building approval. All previous stage boundaries were managed by project manager Simona Kralova using the Managing a stage boundary process. Simona plans that at the end of this stage too she will first carry out SB, prepare an end stage report and ask the Project Board to approve it, and only then start closing the project.
question: Was Simona's plan appropriate, and why?
options: No, because SB is not carried out at the end of the last stage; instead, the Project manager starts Closing a project directly.
No, because SB is carried out only at the end of the initiation stage and is no longer used at the boundaries of later stages.
Yes, because SB is carried out at the end of every stage and the end stage report of the last stage is an input to Closing a project.
Yes, because the Project Board approves the results of the last stage in the activity “Authorize a stage or exception plan”.
explanation: Managing a stage boundary is used at the end of initiation and of every subsequent stage except the last; towards the end of the last stage, the “project end approaching” trigger in CS leads directly to the Closing a project process. The performance of the last stage and of the whole project is therefore evaluated by the end project report, not the end stage report. The exception is an exception plan – because of it, SB is used at any time, even in the last stage.

scenario: The Krokus Mobil project of the regional Krokus Bank is in its last delivery stage. The Project Board received an exception report: because of a new statutory accessibility requirement for the application, the stage will be extended by six weeks, which exceeds the stage tolerance but not the project tolerance. The board asked for an exception plan. Project manager Tomas Vesely objects that the Managing a stage boundary process is not used in the last stage, and proposes just recording the changes in the issue register and carrying on.
question: How should Tomas proceed according to PRINCE2?
options: Prepare the exception plan in the Managing a stage boundary process, which is used for exception plans even in the last stage.
Continue according to the original stage plan and explain the deviation from the plan in the end project report in the Closing a project process.
Start the Closing a project process and prepare the exception plan within it, because in the last stage CP replaces the SB process.
Ask the business layer for a new tolerance, because in the last stage the exception plan is always approved by the business layer.
explanation: An exception plan is prepared in the Managing a stage boundary process (activity “Prepare exception plan”) at the board's request – in any stage, including the last. The board then approves it in DP in the activity “Authorize a stage or exception plan”. Because the deviation does not exceed the project tolerance, the Project Board decides, not the business layer, and it is not possible to continue without dealing with the exceeded stage tolerance.
