scenario: The Lipa Klub loyalty programme of the Drogerie Lipa chain is in its second stage, whose stage plan has a time tolerance of ±2 weeks. Project manager Alena Cermakova found that the platform supplier LoyalTech will not deliver the e-shop interface on time and the stage will be delayed by five weeks. Alena immediately drew up an exception plan with a new schedule and submitted it to the Project Board for approval in order to “save one round of meetings”.
question: Was Alena's action appropriate, and why?
options: No, because she should first have submitted an exception report with options and a recommendation; an exception plan is prepared only at the board's request.
No, because when the supplier is late, the Senior supplier prepares the exception plan himself, as he is responsible for supplier resources.
Yes, because the exception plan is the Project manager's responsibility and is always prepared in SB whenever a tolerance is threatened to be exceeded.
Yes, because submitting a finished plan is quicker and the board can approve it straight away in the activity “Give ad hoc direction”.
explanation: The procedure for an exception has two steps: in CS the Project manager forecasts that the stage tolerance will be exceeded and submits an exception report with the cause, impacts, options and a recommendation; in DP the board decides – it may request an exception plan, but it may also choose another option. Only at its request does the Project manager prepare the exception plan in SB, and the board approves it in “Authorize a stage or exception plan” (“Give ad hoc direction” is moreover a name from the 6th edition). A finished plan without a board decision pre-empts a choice that belongs to the board.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set from the top down and exceptions are escalated from the bottom up.

scenario: During excavation for the new laboratory pavilion of Polabska University, archaeological finds were discovered. Project manager Simona Kralova submitted an exception report to the Project Board: the project will be extended by seven months and cost CZK 40 million more, which exceeds the project tolerance set by the rector (business layer). Executive Karel Novak proposes that the board itself request an exception plan and approve it once it is complete.
question: How should the Project Board proceed according to PRINCE2?
options: Pass the situation to the business layer, because the project tolerance was set by the rector and he decides on its being exceeded.
Follow the Executive, because the Project Board always approves exception plans itself in “Authorize a stage or exception plan”.
Instruct Simona to amend the project plan as part of the activity “Take corrective action” and continue working according to the amended plan.
Immediately issue a premature close request, because exceeding the project tolerance means loss of the project's justification.
explanation: Project tolerance is set by the business layer, and therefore its forecast breach is escalated to it: the Project Board passes the exception report to the rector, who decides on the further course of action (for example an exception plan that will replace the project plan, or termination of the project). The board itself decides only on exceptions within the project's tolerances, typically at stage level. Premature closure is one of the options, not an automatic consequence of exceeding tolerance.

image.alt: Chain of business layer, Project Board, Project manager and Team manager: tolerances are set from the top down and exceptions are escalated from the bottom up.

scenario: In the activity “Authorize a stage or exception plan”, the Project Board of the Krokus Mobil project of the regional Krokus Bank approved an exception plan for the second stage, which addresses a six-week delay caused by a regulatory requirement. The original stage plan assumed the stage would be completed in March, the exception plan in May. Project manager Tomas Vesely asks against which plan he should report progress in highlight reports from now on.
question: What applies, according to PRINCE2, to the further management of the stage?
options: The exception plan replaces the existing stage plan, and Tomas continues to manage the stage in Controlling a stage and reports progress against it.
The stage plan remains the stage baseline and the exception plan is merely an attachment that Tomas uses to explain deviations in highlight reports.
The exception plan replaces the project plan, and the board must therefore re-authorise the whole project in the activity “Authorize the project”.
The stage tolerances cease to apply and until the end of the stage Tomas follows the Executive's instructions directly in the activity “Give ongoing direction”.
explanation: An exception plan replaces the plan whose tolerances would be exceeded – for a stage-level exception, therefore, the stage plan. After board approval, the stage continues to be managed in Controlling a stage according to the exception plan, and highlight reports compare actual performance with it. A project-level exception plan would replace the project plan; here it is a stage exception, and no new authorisation of the whole project is required.

image.alt: Levels of plans in PRINCE2 7: project plan, stage plan, optional team plan and exception plan, which replaces the project plan or a stage plan.

scenario: The second stage of construction of the new laboratory pavilion of Polabska University is nearing its end and project manager Simona Kralova is starting the Managing a stage boundary process. During the stage the university obtained a European grant, thanks to which the pavilion will be used by two more research teams, and at the same time construction materials became considerably more expensive. Simona wants to submit only the third-stage stage plan to the Project Board, because “the business case was prepared in initiation and the project plan will not change because of this”.
question: Was Simona's decision appropriate, and why?
options: No, because in SB she should also update the project plan and the business case so that the board can assess the continued business justification of the project.
No, because at the stage boundary the Senior user should update the business case, while the Project manager prepares only plans.
Yes, because after the PID is approved the business case is updated only when the Project Board requests an exception plan because of a forecast exception.
Yes, because changes in benefits and costs are assessed only in Closing a project, as part of the activity “Evaluate the project”.
explanation: At the stage boundary, SB contains the activities “Update the project plan” and “Update the business case”: the plan is updated with actuals and the forecast (here the more expensive materials) and the business case with the new costs and benefits (here the grant). On that basis the board then confirms the continued business justification of the project in “Authorize a stage or exception plan”. The stage plan of the next stage alone is not enough for such a decision.

scenario: At the end of the second stage of the Krokus Mobil project of the regional Krokus Bank, Project manager Tomas Vesely is preparing the end stage report. During the stage it turned out that early involvement of the compliance department had halved the time needed to approve new features, and the IT director would like to use this experience immediately in two bank projects that are just starting. Tomas therefore prepared, within SB, a brief lessons report in addition to the end stage report and submitted it to the Project Board with a proposal to pass it on to the management of both new projects.
question: Was Tomas's action appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because a lessons report can also be prepared at the end of a stage as part of “Evaluate the stage”, if a lesson is useful immediately.
Yes, because a lessons report at the end of a stage replaces the lessons log, which is thereby closed for that stage.
No, because a lessons report is produced only once, in the Closing a project process as part of the activity “Evaluate the project”.
No, because passing lessons on to other projects of the organisation is the responsibility of the business layer, not the Project manager.
explanation: In SB, the activity “Evaluate the stage” (in the 6th edition “Report stage end”) includes preparing the end stage report and, as needed, a lessons report – this is not produced only when the project is closed, but whenever it is useful to pass lessons on to the organisation. The principle Learn from experience requires lessons not only to be recorded but also to be applied in good time. The lessons log continues to be kept in the project log; the lessons report does not replace it, it only passes the lessons on.

scenario: At the end of the second stage of the Lipa Klub loyalty programme (Drogerie Lipa chain), project manager Alena Cermakova completed the Managing a stage boundary process. In the activity “Request next stage” she handed the Project Board the end stage report, the updated project plan, the updated business case and the stage plan of the third stage. Executive Michal Svoboda is preparing the board's meeting agenda.
question:
Which two decisions belong to the Project Board in the activity “Authorize a stage or exception plan”?
1. Confirm that the project is still justified.
2. Set the tolerances of the individual work packages of the third stage.
3. Approve the stage plan of the third stage and set the tolerances of that stage.
4. Adjust the project tolerances according to the updated project plan.
options: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: In “Authorize a stage or exception plan”, the board reviews the end stage report, the updated business case and project plan, confirms the continued business justification of the project, approves the stage plan of the next stage and sets tolerances for it. Work package tolerances are set by the Project manager when authorising them in Controlling a stage, and project tolerances are set by the business layer, so the board cannot adjust them on its own.

scenario: At Polabska University, the first delivery stage of the new laboratory pavilion project is ending; during it, the public tender for the construction took place. It was won by the company StavPol, whose construction director will be responsible for supplier resources and the technical quality of the construction in the following stages. Until now, supplier interests in the Project Board were represented by the head of the university's technical department. Project manager Simona Kralova is starting the Managing a stage boundary process.
question: How should the change on the supplier side be reflected in the management of the project in SB?
options: Review the team structure and role descriptions in the PID and involve a StavPol representative as Senior supplier, because the supplier has changed.
Leave the structure of the project management team unchanged, as appointed in SU, and not change it for the entire duration of the project.
Invite a StavPol representative to board meetings only as a guest, because the PID is never updated after the project is authorised.
Merely describe the change in the end stage report and update the team structure only in the Closing a project process as part of “Evaluate the project”.
explanation: The objectives of SB include reviewing and updating the PID, including the structure of the project management team and role descriptions; a stage boundary is the natural place to adapt the project organisation to a new situation, for example the selection of an external supplier. The Senior supplier is to represent those who provide resources and are responsible for the technical quality of the products – in the following stages, therefore, StavPol. The PID is a baseline that is regularly reviewed at stage boundaries, so the claim that it does not change after authorisation is not valid.

scenario: The Krokus Mobil application of the regional Krokus Bank has been launched and the project is in the Closing a project process. The Senior user confirmed that the products meet the acceptance criteria. The bank's IT operations department, however, refuses to take over support of the application, because the supplier AppNest has neither handed over the operational documentation nor trained its staff; once the project team is released, nobody would support the application. Project manager Tomas Vesely nevertheless wants to ask the Project Board for project closure immediately, so that the release of the team is not delayed.
question: Was it appropriate to ask for project closure in this situation, and why?
options: No, because before closure it must be ensured that the organisation is able to operate and support the products after the project.
No, because project closure is requested by the Senior user, who is responsible for acceptance and for taking the products into operation.
Yes, because the only condition for closure is acceptance of the products by users; ensuring operational support is a matter for normal operations.
Yes, because an unresolved handover can be stated in the follow-on action recommendations and operations can be settled only after the project is closed.
explanation: The objectives of Closing a project include not only verifying acceptance by users but also ensuring that the organisation is able to support and operate the products after the project ends. If operations refuses the handover and nobody would support the application once the team is released, the project is not ready for closure and the handover must be completed, or the situation escalated to the board. Follow-on action recommendations serve to hand over open issues and risks, not to bypass a missing handover.

scenario: The Lipa Klub loyalty programme of the Drogerie Lipa chain has been launched in all stores and project manager Alena Cermakova is preparing the end project report in the Closing a project process. The issue register still contains three change requests whose implementation the board postponed (for example points for returned packaging), and the risk register contains an open risk that a new version of the checkout software will disrupt the loading of loyalty cards.
question: How should Alena deal with these open items?
options: State them in the follow-on action recommendations so that, after the project is closed, the designated owners in the organisation take them over.
Close them in the registers as rejected, because after the project ends nobody maintains the issue register or the risk register any more.
Ask the board for another delivery stage, because the project cannot be closed while open items remain in the registers.
Record them in the lessons report, which the board will pass to the business layer as input for planning future projects.
explanation: The objective of CP is to ensure that unclosed issues and risks are not lost: the Project manager hands them over in the form of follow-on action recommendations, which are part of the end project report, and after the project the designated owners in the organisation take them over. Open items are not a reason to prolong the project or to reject them administratively. A lessons report captures lessons, not tasks that need to be settled after the project.

scenario: The goal of the Krokus Mobil project of the regional Krokus Bank is to raise the share of clients actively using mobile banking from 35% to 60%, within 18 months of the launch of the new application. The application has been in operation for three months, the share has reached 41% and the project is in the Closing a project process. In the end project report, Project manager Tomas Vesely evaluated the benefits achieved so far, updated the benefits management approach with benefit reviews at 12 and 18 months after launch, and then asked the Project Board to close the project.
question: Was Tomas's action appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because in CP the benefits achieved so far are assessed and the benefits management approach is updated with benefit reviews that will take place after the project.
Yes, because after the project is closed nobody is responsible for benefits any more and planned reviews are merely a recommendation.
No, because the project can be closed only after all benefits have been confirmed, otherwise the principle Ensure continued business justification would not be followed.
No, because the Project Board plans post-project benefit reviews only after issuing the closure notice, not the Project manager in CP.
explanation: Many benefits materialise only after the project ends. In CP (activity “Evaluate the project”), the benefits achieved so far are therefore assessed and the benefits management approach is updated with post-project benefit reviews; in “Authorize project closure” the board verifies that they are planned. The Senior user remains responsible for realising the benefits and the business layer ensures the post-project reviews, so waiting with closure until the target 60% is reached would needlessly tie up project resources.

scenario: The new laboratory pavilion of Polabska University has passed final building approval and been handed over to the faculties, Senior user Prof. Hana Cerna has confirmed acceptance and project manager Simona Kralova has completed the end project report. Because the Project Board will meet only in three weeks, Simona herself sent stakeholders a notice of project closure, terminated the contracts with external specialists and sent the end project report to the board “for information”.
question: Was Simona's action appropriate, and why?
options: No, because she should have asked the board for closure; closure is authorised and the closure notice is issued only by the Project Board.
No, because the closure notice is issued by the business layer and she should have sent the end project report directly to the rector.
Yes, because after the Senior user's acceptance of the products, closing the project is within the Project manager's authority.
Yes, because in the activity “Recommend project closure” the Project manager closes the project and the board is merely informed of it.
explanation: In CP, the Project manager prepares closure and in the activity “Request project closure” (in the 6th edition “Recommend project closure”) asks the board to authorise it. In DP (“Authorize project closure”), the Project Board verifies acceptance, approves the end project report and the lessons report and issues the closure notice, by which the project is formally ended and its resources are released. Acceptance of the products by the user is a precondition for closure, but it does not give the Project manager the authority to close the project on his own.

scenario: In the third stage of the Lipa Klub loyalty programme, the board of directors of the Drogerie Lipa chain decided on a merger with a competitor that has its own loyalty programme. The Project Board therefore sent a premature close request to project manager Alena Cermakova. The application is 60% complete, the checkout integration works in the pilot stores and the supplier LoyalTech has further modules in progress.
question: What should Alena do in the Closing a project process?
options: Establish the status of the products, ensure the handover of those that have value, record lessons and prepare follow-on action recommendations.
Immediately stop all work, terminate the contracts with suppliers and close the project without further evaluation, so that no unnecessary costs are incurred.
Complete the modules in progress, so that “Confirm project acceptance” can be carried out according to the original project product description.
Prepare an exception plan for the remaining part of the project in the Managing a stage boundary process and submit it to the board for approval.
explanation: Premature closure (activity “Prepare premature closure”) is an orderly, not a chaotic, ending: the Project manager establishes and records the status of the products, ensures that products with value (here, for example, the functional checkout integration) are handed over or preserved, and prepares an end project report with follow-on action recommendations as well as a lessons report. Completing work according to the original scope or preparing an exception plan makes no sense – the board has already decided on closure.

scenario: In the middle of the third stage of the Krokus Mobil project, the main supplier AppNest announced insolvency. Krokus Bank's Project manager Tomas Vesely estimates that with a replacement supplier the project would become considerably more expensive and the business case would cease to be viable. Tomas therefore stopped all work packages and started the Closing a project process; he intends to inform the board of this in the next highlight report.
question: Was Tomas's action appropriate, and why?
options: No, because he should have escalated the situation with an exception report; Closing a project is triggered only by a premature close request from the board.
No, because when the project's justification is lost, the Project manager should first prepare an exception plan with a replacement supplier himself.
Yes, because according to the principle Ensure continued business justification the Project manager immediately ends a project that is not justified.
Yes, because the supplier's insolvency is an event external to the project, in which the Project manager may start Closing a project on his own.
explanation: A forecast that costs will exceed tolerances and the business case will cease to be viable is an exception: in CS the Project manager escalates it with an exception report containing options and a recommendation. Premature closure is decided by the Project Board (after consulting the business layer as needed), which issues a premature close request in DP (“Give ongoing direction”), and only that triggers Closing a project. The principle Ensure continued business justification requires a project without justification to be stopped, but the decision belongs to the board, not the Project manager.
